Park Jr. is someone who paid to use the name or actually a son of Adolfo Tapia. {{endplainlist}} |relatives ={{plainlist}} *[[El Hijo de Cien Caras]] (brother) *[[Super Parka]] (uncle) *Johnny Ibara (uncle) *Desalmado (uncle) *[[Volador Jr.]] (nephew) *[[Flyer (wrestler)|Flyer]] (great nephew){{cite web | url=http://superluchas.com/2014/01/14/flyer-el-tercer-volador-esta-aqui/ | title=Flyer, el tercer Volador está aquí | date=February 14, 2014 | access-date=May 23, 2015 | work=[[Súper Luchas]] | language=es | trans-title=Flyer, the third Volador is here}} {{endplainlist}} |billed=[[Monclova]], [[Coahuila]], Mexico |trainer=Raul Reyes
Alberto Mora |debut=1982 |retired=}} '''Adolfo Margarito Tapia Ibarra''' (November 14, 1965) is a Mexican [[Professional wrestling|professional wrestler]], who currently performs as '''L. A. Park'''. He is best known throughout the world as the original '''La Parka''', especially from his many years in the American [[World Championship Wrestling]] promotion. He has worked for every major and multiple minor wrestling promotions in Mexico, as well as participating on multiple wrestling tours in [[Japan]]. He is a three-time [[World heavyweight wrestling championship|world heavyweight champion]], having held the [[IWC World Heavyweight Championship|IWC World Heavyweight]], IWC World Hardcore, and [[IWL World Heavyweight Championship|IWL World Heavyweight]] championships all once. He is also a two-time [[World tag team championship|world tag team champion]], having held the [[MLW World Tag Team Championship]] and the [[CMLL World Tag Team Championship]] each once. Tapia was forced to change his [[ring name]] from "La Parka" to "L.A. Park" (short for ''La Auténtica Park''; "The Original Park") in early 2003 when AAA owner [[Antonio Peña]] asserted his copyright claims to the La Parka character, barring Tapia from using the name as he promoted his own version of the gimmick with this new wrestler also being known as [[La Parka (wrestler, born 1966)|La Parka]]. In March 2010, L.A. Park returned to AAA and started a storyline with AAA's La Parka, pitting the original and the new La Parka against each other. At [[Triplemanía XVIII]], Park defeated La Parka and earned the rights to once again be known as "La Parka". The result, however, was later thrown out. Tapia's uncle changed his character to [[Super Parka]] after Tapia gained worldwide fame. Several of Tapia's other family members are or have been professional wrestlers, including his sons [[El Hijo de L.A. Park]] and [[L.A. Park Jr.]], brother [[El Hijo de Cien Caras]], nephew [[Volador Jr.]], and great nephew [[Flyer (wrestler)|Flyer]], among others. L.A. Park's family is referred to in Mexico as ''La Familia Real''. == Professional wrestling career == === Early career (1982–1992) === Adolfo Tapia made his professional wrestling debut in 1982 at the age of 16, using his real name. Later on he would wrestle as the [[wrestling mask|masked]] ''El Gringo'' in the [[Monclova]], [[Coahuila]] region and as ''El Minero'' in Mexico City. Tapia lost his first ''[[Luchas de Apuestas|Lucha de Apuesta]]'', or bet match, to Climax II and was forced to take off the El Minero [[wrestling mask|mask]] and reveal his real name, as per ''[[lucha libre]]'' (the professional wrestling style originary from Mexico) traditions.{{cite news | author = L.L. Staff | title = Lucha Libre: Conoce la historia de las leyendas de cuadrilátero | work = L.A. Park (1965) | location = Mexico | id = Grandes Figuras de la Lucha Libre | page = 34 | year = 2008 | language = es}} In 1988 he changed his ring character to ''El Asesino de Tepito'' ("The Assassin from Tepito"), a ''[[Heel (professional wrestling)|rudo]]'' (villain) character he used in 1988. He lost the ''Asesino de Tepito'' mask in an ''Apuesta'' match against Astro de Oro at some point in 1988. Following the mask loss Tapia adopted a character called ''Principe Island'' ("Island Prince"), a character he would use until 1992.{{cite book | author= Madigan, Dan | title= Mondo Lucha a Go Go: the bizarre and honorable world of wild Mexican wrestling | publisher= HarperCollins Publishers | year= 2007 | chapter = Los Enmascarados (the masked men): La Parka | pages = 120–125 | isbn=978-0-06-085583-3}} As ''Principe Island'' he won the masks of wrestlers Gran Cóndor, Principe Judas, Guerrero Negra and Bestia Negra I. On November 21, 1987, he lost the ''Principe Island'' mask to [[El Hijo del Santo]]. Following his mask loss he started working as the masked ''Invasor del Norte I'' as well as still taking bookings as ''Principe Island''. The double bookings came to an end on June 26, 1991, when Stuka unmasked the Invasor del Norte character, revealing that Tapia played both characters. === Asistencia Asesoría y Administración (1992–1996) === In 1992 [[Antonio Peña]] founded a new wrestling promotion called [[Asistencia Asesoría y Administración]] (AAA), signing Tapia to a contract early on. Peña came up with the idea to repackage Tapia as "La Parka" (an altered spelling of ''La Parca'', [[Spanish language|Spanish]] for [[Grim Reaper|"The Reaper"]]), a character who wore a full bodysuit and mask that resembled a skeleton like the ones used in Mexico's [[Day of the Dead]] ceremonies. The character was an almost instant success with the fans, the imagery combined with Tapia's charisma and flamboyant actions in the ring made him a big crowd favorite despite La Parka initially being a ''rudo'' character. One of his initial storyline feuds was with [[Lizmark]], a feud that resulted in a match for the [[Mexican National Light Heavyweight Championship]] at AAA's inaugural [[Triplemania I|Triplemanía]] event, in which Lizmark successfully defended the title against La Parka.{{cite web | url = http://www.prowrestlinghistory.com/supercards/mexico/aaa/triple.html#i | title = Asistencia Asesoria y Administracion TripleMania | access-date = February 19, 2009 | publisher = ProWrestlingHistory.com| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20090116004505/http://www.prowrestlinghistory.com/supercards/mexico/aaa/triple.html| archive-date= January 16, 2009 | url-status= live}} In August 1993 La Parka won his first championship when he defeated Lizmark for the [[WWA Light Heavyweight Championship]] on a WWA/AAA co-promoted show. The title reign lasted until October 23, 1993, when Lizmark won the title back. The feud between the two saw La Parka defeat Lizmark for the WWA title for a second time on June 20, 1994. La Parka was one of the wrestlers that worked the ''[[AAA When Worlds Collide|When Worlds Collide]]'' show, a joint AAA/[[World Championship Wrestling]] (WCW) [[pay-per-view]] where he teamed with [[Jerry Estrada]] and [[Blue Panther]], losing to the team of [[Chris Benoit|The Pegasus Kid]], [[2 Cold Scorpio]], and [[Tito Santana]].{{cite news|title=Historical Cards|work=PWI Presents: 2007 Wrestling Almanak and book of facts|publisher=Kappa Publications|id=2007 Edition|page=160}} On September 9, 1994, La Parka won the Mexican National Light Heavyweight Championship that he had been chasing for over a year when he defeated Lizmark for the title, finishing off the storyline between the two. La Parka held the title for 200 days losing it to Jerry Estrada. La Parka would wear the Mexican National Light Heavyweight championship two further times while working for AAA, in 1995 and in 1996 until he lost the belt to [[Pimpinela Escarlata]] on May 13, 1996. === Extreme Championship Wrestling (1995) === In 1995 he would make an appearance for [[Extreme Championship Wrestling]] (ECW) in the United States, teaming with [[Psicosis]], losing a tag team match against [[Konnan]] and [[Rey Mysterio Jr.|Rey Misterio Jr.]]. === World Championship Wrestling (1996–2000) === [[Image:LaParka.jpg|thumb|left|270px|La Parka in action]] When WCW began using a number of AAA wrestlers for their [[Cruiserweight (professional wrestling)|cruiserweight]] division in mid to late 1996, La Parka gained worldwide exposure by appearing on WCW's weekly television shows and PPVs. La Parka often wrestled against other AAA ''Luchadors'' such as [[Juventud Guerrera]] or [[Super Caló]] and often teamed with Psicosis (known in WCW as Psychosis). Due to La Parka's more comedic style he stood out from the rest of the AAA wrestlers who were generally high fliers. He was nicknamed "the chairman of WCW" due to the fact that he often carried a chair to the ring, played [[air guitar]] on it during his entrances and generally used it both in matches and in post match celebrations.{{cite web|url=http://www.onlineworldofwrestling.com/profiles/l/la-parka.html|title=La Parka profile|publisher=Online World of Wrestling|access-date=August 8, 2009| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20090625220256/http://www.onlineworldofwrestling.com/profiles/l/la-parka.html| archive-date= June 25, 2009 | url-status= live}} At one point he and Psychosis were [[Manager (professional wrestling)|managed]] by [[Sonny Onoo]], although the team failed to achieve much success as a unit. He later dropped Onoo as a manager and begin to feud with Psychosis and [[Disco Inferno (wrestler)|Disco Inferno]]. While La Parka often wrestled on WCW's [[Monday Nitro]] show his PPV appearances were rare. On July 13, he teamed with Psychosis and [[Villano IV]] on the undercard of WCW's [[Bash at the Beach (1997)|Bash at the Beach]] PPV, losing to [[Héctor Garza]], [[Juventud Guerrera]] and [[Lizmark Jr.]]{{cite web | url= http://www.prowrestlinghistory.com/supercards/usa/wcw/beach.html#97 | title= Bash at the Bash 1997 | date= July 13, 1997 | access-date= March 16, 2010 | publisher= Prowrestlinghistory.com | archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20100406041758/http://www.prowrestlinghistory.com/supercards/usa/wcw/beach.html#97 | archive-date= April 6, 2010 | url-status= dead }} He also wrestled at [[SuperBrawl VIII]], losing to Disco Inferno.{{cite web | url=http://www.prowrestlinghistory.com/supercards/usa/wcw/s-brawl.html#VIII | title= SuperBrawl VIII | date= February 22, 1998 | access-date= March 16, 2010 | publisher=Prowrestlinghistory.com}} La Parka's biggest achievement in WCW did not even involve Adolfo Tapia. One night in a match against [[Randy Savage]], La Parka suddenly executed [[Diamond Dallas Page]]'s finisher, the [[Cutter (professional wrestling)|Diamond Cutter]] on Savage and gained the pinfall. After the match "La Parka" unmasked to show that it was in fact Page under the mask, using the ruse to get back at Savage during their rivalry. A couple of weeks later, Savage wrestled against the real La Parka, defeating him to gain a small measure of revenge. In October 1998, La Parka became part of [[Eddie Guerrero]]'s [[Latino World Order]] (LWO), a group that also included Psychosis, Juventud Guerrera, [[Villano IV]], Villano V, [[El Dandy]], [[Silver King (wrestler)|Silver King]], Héctor Garza, [[Damián 666]], and a reluctant Rey Mysterio Jr. The group feuded mainly with Konnan and [[Perry Saturn]]. In January 1999, Guerrero was injured in a car accident and the LWO group was subsequently abandoned. When [[Vince Russo]] and [[Ed Ferrara]] took over the creative portion of WCW in late 1999, the duo had Ferrara's voice [[Dubbing (filmmaking)|dub]] English over the intercom while La Parka would be doing interviews in Spanish. This often ended with a confused [[Gene Okerlund]] exclaiming "What the hell was that?!" Among other things the voice-over explained that La Parka was a fan of [[Skeletor]] from ''[[Masters of the Universe]]'' and other comedic comments. During this time, he teamed with [[Kaz Hayashi]], a Japanese wrestler who also used a "comedic voice over" gimmick and referred to La Parka as "Skull Captain". La Parka left WCW in March 2000 before WCW was bought by WWF a year later. === A second La Parka (1996–2003) === {{See also|La Parka (wrestler)}} After the start of La Parka's WCW run in 1996, AAA debuted a new wrestler, [[La Parka (wrestler)|La Parka Jr.]], who used the same costume. Adolfo Tapia mainly worked for US independent promotions and smaller Mexican promotions during that time, so his continued use of the gimmick did not draw objections. This changed when Tapia signed with AAA's main rival, [[Consejo Mundial de Lucha Libre]], in 2003. AAA owner [[Antonio Peña]] responded by renaming La Parka Jr. and taking legal action to forbid Tapia from performing under the ring name "La Parka" or wearing the character's black-and-white suit.{{cite web | url=http://superluchas.com/la-park-ya-no-podra-vestir-de-blanco-y-negro/ | title= ! LA Park ya no podra vestir de blanco y negro | author=Ocampo, Jorge | date= May 6, 2008 | access-date= March 15, 2010 | work=[[Súper Luchas]] Magazine | language= es}} Tapia responded by counter-suing Peña and making changes to his gimmick, including using the ring name "L.A. ParK", short for "La Autentica ParK" (pronounced "Par-Ka"); a new mask design inspired by the ''[[Star Wars]]'' character [[Darth Maul]]; and new multicolored ring gear. Tapia eventually returned to wearing his black and white bodysuit.{{cite web | url=http://superluchas.com/la-park-de-nuevo-de-blanco-y-negro/ | title= LA Park de nuevo de blanco y negro | author= Ocampo, Jorge | date= July 7, 2008 | access-date= March 15, 2008 | work=[[Súper Luchas]] Magazine | language=es}} === Consejo Mundial de Lucha Libre (2003–2008) === In 2003 L.A. ParK began working for CMLL, although he was often kept off their television broadcasts due to the ongoing legal battles with Peña and AAA. In January 2004 L.A. Park teamed up with [[Shocker (wrestler)|Shocker]] to defeat ''[[Los Guerreros del Infierno]]'' ([[Último Guerrero]] and [[Rey Bucanero]]) to win the [[CMLL World Tag Team Championship]]. Guerrero and Bucanero regained the titles 56 days later, after which L.A. Park challenged Último Guerrero to defend the [[CMLL World Light Heavyweight Championship]] against him at CMLL's [[CMLL 71st Anniversary Show|71st Anniversary Show]], a match which L.A. Park lost two falls to one.{{cite news | author = Ocampo, Jorge | title = Aniversario 71 de CMLL | work =[[Súper Luchas]]| id = issue 72 | date = September 26, 2004 | language = es}} Tapia worked for CMLL in an on-again, off-again capacity, not being booked for CMLL for long stretches of time. During one of those "off again" periods, L.A. Park won the Mexican National Light Heavyweight Championship for the fourth time when he defeated El Dandy for the title on October 15, 2004, making him one of only two wrestlers to hold the title four times. In early 2007 La Parka returned to CMLL full-time and began a storyline with [[Perro Aguayo Jr.]], a storyline that saw the two face off in a singles match at the 2007 ''[[Sin Piedad (2007)|Sin Piedad]]'' event where L.A. Park won by disqualification after ''[[Los Perros del Mal]]'' interfered in the match.{{cite news | author = Ocampo, Jorge | title = Rapo a Black Warrior y Rey Bucanero | work =[[Súper Luchas]]| id = issue 242 | date = December 9, 2007 | pages=3–6 | url=http://Superluchas.com/super-luchas-242/ | access-date = February 26, 2007 | language = es}} The storyline ended in mid-2008 with no satisfactory end, instead L.A. Park began a feud with [[Dr. Wagner Jr.]] Initially, L.A. Park was the ''tecnico'' in the feud, but the fan reactions began to turn against L.A. Park as the CMLL crowd began siding with Dr. Wagner Jr. This led to a double turn between the competitors. Playing the ''Rudo'' L.A. Park was disqualified several times for excessive violence, including a match at the [[CMLL 75th Anniversary Show]] that L.A. Park lost by disqualification.{{cite news | author = Arturo Rosas Plata | title = Acabó con la leyenda de Panther | url = http://itecor.v1.myvirtualpaper.com/20092008/2008092001/en/?page=21 | work = Ovaciones | publisher = Editorial Ovaciones, S. A. de C.V. | location = [[Mexico]], [[Mexican Federal District|D.F.]] | id = Número 21353 Año LXI | page = 21 | date = September 20, 2008 | access-date = September 19, 2009 | language = es | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20120222094136/http://itecor.v1.myvirtualpaper.com/20092008/2008092001/en/?page=21 | archive-date = February 22, 2012 | url-status = dead }} In the months following the Anniversary show both L.A. Park and Dr. Wagner Jr. left CMLL. === Independent circuit (2000–present) === [[File:Conrad Kennedy III vs. La Parka black and white.jpg|thumb|LA Parka in 2007]] While working for CMLL La Parka was allowed to also wrestle for independent promotions in Mexico, the US and Japan. During his time on the independent circuit L.A. Park developed a long-running and very intense feud with [[El Hijo del Santo]] and [[Blue Demon Jr.]], interjecting himself in a storyline that played off the original rivalry between [[El Santo]] and [[Blue Demon]] creating a feud that headlined various shows all over Mexico and involves three of the most famous masks of the 1980s and 1990s.{{cite book | author= Various | title= Lucha Libre: Masked Superstars of Mexican Wrestling | publisher= Distributed Art Publishers, Inc. | year= 2005 | chapter = Leyenda vs Leyenda vs... / Legend Vs Legends Vs ... | pages = 297–304 | isbn=968-6842-48-9}} In 2004, Tapia made a number of appearances for [[Total Nonstop Action Wrestling]] (TNA), as both L.A. Park and La Parka. He wrestled in a [[Gauntlet for the Gold]] for the [[TNA X Division Championship]] at one of TNA's weekly PPVs and then appeared in yet another X Division gauntlet match at TNA's inaugural monthly PPV [[Victory Road (2004)|Victory Road]], losing on both occasions.{{cite web|url=http://www.prowrestlinghistory.com/supercards/usa/misc/tna/victory.html#2004| title=Victory Road 2004 at Pro Wrestling History.com|access-date=March 15, 2010 |publisher=Pro Wrestling History.com}} On May 7, 2005, L.A. Park debuted for Detroit's Independent Wrestling Revolution (IWR) brand ''Revolucha'', teaming with American Kickboxer in a losing effort to El Hijo del Santo and Konnan. Park continued his rivalry with El Hijo del Santo culminating on October 29, 2005, at ''Revolucha 2: Dia de los Muertos'' in a ''Lucha en la Jaula'' match (a steel cage match). Both Park and Santo had their masks ripped apart and were bleeding profusely during the match. In February 2006, L.A. Park began a bitter feud with then IWR Champion Conrad Kennedy III (CK3). L.A. Park finally defeated CK3 on August 27, 2006, at ''Brawl at the Hall 6'' and defended the IWR Heavyweight Championship on October 14, 2007, at ''Revolucha 4''. After leaving CMLL in 2008 L.A. Park worked regularly for the newly started ''[[Perros del Mal (promotion)|Perros del Mal Producciones]]'', reviving his old rivalry with Perro Aguayo Jr. Working on the ''Perros del Mal'' shows also allowed Tapia to help his son make his start in the wrestling business. Originally Tapia's son wrestled as "Black Spirit" without acknowledging the relationship between L.A. Park and Black Spirit. In early 2010 Tapia officially acknowledge that Black Spirit was his son announcing that he would wrestle as [[El Hijo de L.A. Park]] ("The Son of L.A. Park") from then. In 2011, Tapia was part of [[Lucha Libre USA]] as '''LA Park'''. === Xtreme Latin American Wrestling (2004, 2009–2010) === L.A. Park won the Xtreme Latin American Wrestling (X-LAW) Heavyweight Championship in Friday, April 9, 2004. The bout was a decision match for the vacant title against [[Rey Misterio]] in a X-LAW show co-promoted with Baja Stars Wrestling in Auditorio Fausto Gutiérrez Moreno, in [[Tijuana]]. In subsequent years, X-LAW closed down, leaving L.A. Park as the last X-LAW Heavyweight Champion. In 2009, X-LAW's owner, Ernesto Ocampo, [[Súper Luchas]] Magazine publisher, decided to restart his promotion,{{cite web|url=http://luchawiki.org/index.php?title=XLAW |title=X-LAW |publisher=Luchawiki |date=March 24, 2017 |access-date=May 31, 2019}} promoting the return show on August 8, 2009, headlined with Tapia against [[The Sandman (wrestler)|The Sandman]] for the title.{{cite web | url= http://Superluchas.com/33187/ | title= Resultados XLAW: Sandman vs LA Park (8 agosto 2009) – LA Park retiene en encuentro memorable – Súper Crazy aparece por sorpresa | author= Ocampo, Jorge | date= August 9, 2009 | access-date= March 15, 2010 | work=[[Súper Luchas]] Magazine | language=es}} Tapia hyped the show in Ocampo's magazine and website weeks in advance as a "return to the Hardcore style" of ECW.{{cite web | url=http://superluchas.com/la-gente-en-mexico-esta-acostumbrada-a-quebrarse-foquitos-romperse-lamparitas-atte-la-park/ | title= La gente en Mexico esta acostumbrada a quebrarse foquitos romperse lamparitas - atte: LA Park | author= Ocampo, Jorge | date= July 22, 2009 | access-date= March 15, 2010 | work=[[Súper Luchas]] Magazine | language=es}} The next show was on March 20, 2010, with L.A. Park facing [[Sabu (wrestler)|Sabu]] in the main event.{{cite web | url= http://superluchas.com/cartel-xlaw-20-marzo-en-tula-hidalgo-%C2%BFquien-es-el-luchador-sorpresa/ | title= Cartel XLAW 20 marzo en Tula, Hidalgo – ¿Quién es el luchador sorpresa? | date= March 2, 2010 | access-date= March 16, 2010 | author= Ocampo, Jorge | work=[[Súper Luchas]] Magazine | language=es| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20100309094353/http://superluchas.com/2010/03/02/cartel-xlaw-20-marzo-en-tula-hidalgo-%C2%BFquien-es-el-luchador-sorpresa/| archive-date= March 9, 2010 | url-status= live}} [[Super Parka]] was the special referee. L.A. Park beat Sabu after Super Parka hit Tapia with a steel chair, he fell on top of Sabu for the win. Super Parka then took the belt and ran off with it.{{cite web | url= http://superluchas.com/resultados-x-law-20-marzo-10-super-parka-se-lleva-el-campeonato-completo-la-hermandad-187-aparece-en-x-law/ | title= Resultados X-LAW (20 marzo 10): Súper Parka se lleva el Campeonato Completo… La Hermandad 187 aparece en X-LAW | author= Velazquez, Israel | date= March 20, 2010 | access-date= December 30, 2010 | work=[[Súper Luchas]] Magazine | language=es}} This storyline is unresolved, because after Tapia jump to AAA, in subsequent X-LAW shows, Sabu has been promoted as X-LAW top star. On October 30, 2010, Sabu defeated [[Damián 666]] to win Xtreme Latin American Wrestling's International Championship.,{{cite web|url=http://superluchas.com/2010/10/30/resultados-x-law-hardcoreween-30-octubre-2010/|title=Resultados X-LAW: HARDCOREWEEN (30 octubre 2010) – Sabú termina con una costilla rota|author=Ocampo, Jorge|work=[[Súper Luchas]]magazine|date=October 30, 2010|access-date=November 1, 2010|language=es}} but no word about the fate of the Heavyweight title. === Return to AAA (2010–2013) === [[File:La parka.jpg|thumb|right|La Parka during a wrestling match]] On March 12, 2010, during the 2010 ''[[Rey de Reyes (2010)|Rey de Reyes]]'' event Dorian Roldan, son of AAA boss Joaquin Roldan announced that he, Dorian, was going to take control of the promotion and that he had some help to do so. That help turned out to be L.A. Park, the original La Parka returning to AAA after years and years of legal battles and threats. After unveiling himself during the show L.A. Park announced that he was siding with Konnan and Dorian Roldan, targeting the "impostor Parka".{{cite web|url=http://www.luchalibreaaa.com/coberturaenvivordr.html |title=Rey de Reyes, cobertura en vivo aqui |date=March 12, 2010 |access-date=March 13, 2010 |publisher=[[Asistencia Asesoría y Administración|AAA]] |language=es |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100317144244/http://www.luchalibreaaa.com/coberturaenvivordr.html |archive-date=March 17, 2010 |url-status=dead }} In order to maintain the illusion that L.A. Park did not really work for AAA, L.A. Park claimed that he came to AAA to beat up La Parka, and since he had done that already he was not sure if he even felt like returning to AAA.{{cite news | author = Rivera, Luis Manuel | title = LA Park: Habla de AAA y Súper Parka | work =[[Súper Luchas]]| id = issue 359 | pages= 24–25 | date = April 12, 2010 | language = es}} L.A. Park did however return to an AAA ring as he had another brawl with La Parka on their April 18 television taping. During the event La Parka challenged L.A. Park to a match at [[Triplemanía XVIII]], under any stipulation the original Parka wanted.{{cite web | url=http://www.luchalibreaaa.com/orizabacronica.html | title= El licenciado Roldan ¡Atacado! | author= LuchaLibreAAA staff | date= April 18, 2010 | access-date= April 19, 2010 | publisher= [[Asistencia Asesoría y Administración|AAA]] | language=es| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20100422200536/http://www.luchalibreaaa.com/orizabacronica.html| archive-date= April 22, 2010 | url-status= live}} During AAA's television taping on April 30, 2010, L.A. Park accepted La Parka's challenge for a match at Triplemanía XVIII.{{cite web | url= http://superluchas.com/aaa-en-queretaro-resultados-30-de-abril-las-parkas-se-destrozan-octagon-nuevo-wagnermaniaco-debuta-daniels-una-lucha-mas-para-triplemania-18/ | title= AAA En Querétaro (resultados 30 de abril) – "Las Parkas" se destrozan- Octagon Nuevo Wagnermaniaco – Debuta Daniels – Una lucha mas para Triplemania 18 | author= Ruiz Glez, Alex | date= May 1, 2010 | access-date= May 2, 2010 | work=[[Súper Luchas]] Magazine | language=es| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20100503054037/http://superluchas.com/2010/05/01/aaa-en-queretaro-resultados-30-de-abril-las-parkas-se-destrozan-octagon-nuevo-wagnermaniaco-debuta-daniels-una-lucha-mas-para-triplemania-18/| archive-date= May 3, 2010 | url-status= live}} At an AAA press conference on May 12, 2010, it was announced that the match between the two would be for the rights to the name "La Parka".{{cite web | url=http://superluchas.com/lo-destacado-en-la-conferencia-de-prensa-aaa-previo-a-triplemania-18/ | title= Lo destacado en la conferencia de prensa AAA, previo a Triplemania 18. | date= May 12, 2010 | access-date= May 13, 2010 | author= Ruiz Glez, Alex | work=[[Súper Luchas]] Magazine | language=es| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20100516172814/http://superluchas.com/2010/05/12/lo-destacado-en-la-conferencia-de-prensa-aaa-previo-a-triplemania-18/| archive-date= May 16, 2010 | url-status= live}} At Triplemanía XVIII L.A. Park faced La Parka in the main event of the show. Near the end of the match Park used a [[tombstone piledriver]], a move that is illegal in Lucha Libre. Joaquin Roldan entered the ring, when L.A. Park attempted to use a steel chair on La Parka. When L.A. Park teased using the chair on Joaquin instead, Dorian entered the ring to protest, but was pushed down by Park, who then hit Joaquin with the chair, which caused Dorian to turn on him, hitting him with a steel chair three times. [[Halloween (wrestler)|Halloween]] and [[Damián 666]] from the [[Perros del Mal (promotion)|Perros del Mal]] wrestling promotion run to the ring to chase Dorian Roldan away. Then they drag L.A. Park on top of La Parka before ''rúdo'' referee Hijo del Tirantes counts for three to give L.A. Park the victory. After the bell rings the rest of ''Los Perros del Mal'', (including Park's son Hijo de L.A. Park) came to the ring to celebrate with L.A. Park who had won the rights to the name "La Parka". After a couple of minutes a group of AAA wrestlers led by [[Octagón]] came to ringside and in combination with the arena security managed to remove Los Perros del Mal from the ring. La Parka was taken from the ring on a stretcher, not having moved since L.A. Park applied the piledriver. A bit later it was announced that the match results had been thrown out due to interference by Los Perros del Mal, but the following morning it was confirmed that Tapia had indeed won and would now be known as "La Parka" once again.{{cite web | url= http://superluchas.com/triplemania-18-cobertura-y-resultados-6-junio-2010-la-parka-vs-l-a-park-electroshock-vs-dr-wagner-jr-los-perros-del-mal-en-aaa/ | title= Triplemania 18 (Cobertura y resultados 6 junio 2010) – La Parka vs. L.A. Park – Electroshock vs. Dr. Wagner Jr. – Los Perros del Mal en AAA | author= Marquina, Alva | date= June 6, 2010 | access-date= June 6, 2010 | work=[[Súper Luchas]] Magazine | language=es}}{{cite web|url=http://www.luchalibreaaa.com/triplemaniaxviii.html|title=Triplemania XVIII: Fiesta de Fiestas |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100815092851/http://www.luchalibreaaa.com/triplemaniaxviii.html|archive-date=August 15, 2010|date=June 7, 2010|access-date=June 8, 2010|language=es|publisher=[[Asistencia Asesoría y Administración]]}} However, on June 10 AAA announced that it would respect Mexico City Boxing and Wrestling Commission's decision to throw out the match and as a result both L.A. Park and La Parka would keep their names.{{cite web | url=http://superluchas.com/aaa-acepta-la-decision-de-la-comision-de-lucha-libre-del-df-la-lucha-de-las-parkas-queda-anulada/ | title= AAA acepta la decisión de la comisión de Lucha Libre del DF: La lucha de las Parkas queda anulada | author= Ruiz Glez, Alex | date= June 11, 2010 | access-date= June 17, 2010 | work=[[Súper Luchas]] Magazine | language=es}} Park stated that for him the Triplemanía match was all about pride and not about names and that all that mattered to him was that he had proven who the true La Parka is, regardless of the names they now go by.{{cite web | url= http://usa.record.com.mx/node/3693 | title= L.A. Park deshecha el nombre de La Parka | author= Montiel, César | date= June 8, 2010 | access-date= June 18, 2010 | publisher= Record.com.mx | language= es | url-status= dead | archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20110901005021/http://usa.record.com.mx/node/3693 | archive-date= September 1, 2011 }} On July 4 La Parka defeated L.A. Park in a rematch.{{cite web|url=http://www.wrestleview.com/viewnews.php?id=1278693147 |title=Viva La Raza! Lucha Weekly |last=Boutwell |first=Josh |date=July 9, 2010 |access-date=July 22, 2010 |work=WrestleView |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100711071259/http://www.wrestleview.com/viewnews.php?id=1278693147 |archive-date=July 11, 2010 |url-status=dead }} Afterwards, L.A. Park aligned himself with Dorian Roldan's ''[[La Sociedad]]'', a superstable consisting of ''[[Foreign Legion (wrestling)|La Legión Extranjera]]'', ''La Milicia'', ''Los Maniacos'' and the invading ''Los Perros del Mal'' stables.{{cite web|url=http://www.luchalibreaaa.com/dorianroldanlasociedad.html|title=Dorian Roldan: Lider de la Sociedad|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100831095750/http://www.luchalibreaaa.com/dorianroldanlasociedad.html|archive-date=August 31, 2010|date=August 27, 2010|access-date=November 6, 2010|language=es|work=[[Asistencia Asesoría y Administración]]}}{{cite web|url=http://www.luchalibreaaa.com/maniacossociedad.html|title=Maniacos, parte de la Sociedad|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101001084018/http://www.luchalibreaaa.com/maniacossociedad.html|archive-date=October 1, 2010|date=September 27, 2010|access-date=November 6, 2010|language=es|work=[[Asistencia Asesoría y Administración]]}} On December 5 at ''[[Guerra de Titanes (2010)|Guerra de Titanes]]'' L.A. Park defeated [[Ricky Banderas|El Mesías]] to become the number one contender to the [[AAA Mega Championship]], though, at the same event his ''La Sociedad'' stable mate [[El Zorro (wrestler)|El Zorro]] became the new champion by defeating Dr. Wagner Jr.{{cite web | url= http://superluchas.com/aaa-guerra-de-titanes-2010-cobertura-y-resultados-05-de-diciembre-de-2010-%E2%80%93-charly-manson-aparece-y-se-une-a-los-bizzaros/ | title= AAA Guerra de Titanes 2010 (Cobertura y resultados 05 de Diciembre de 2010) – Charly Manson aparece y se une a Los Bizzaros – El Zorro NUEVO Megacampeón AAA | author= Beltrán, William | date= December 5, 2010 | access-date= December 14, 2010 | work=[[Súper Luchas]] Magazine | language= es | url-status= dead | archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20150119211635/http://superluchas.com/aaa-guerra-de-titanes-2010-cobertura-y-resultados-05-de-diciembre-de-2010-%E2%80%93-charly-manson-aparece-y-se-une-a-los-bizzaros/ | archive-date= January 19, 2015 }}{{cite web | url= http://www.luchalibreaaa.com/laparkquiereazorro.html | archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20101227120505/http://www.luchalibreaaa.com/laparkquiereazorro.html | title= L.A. Park quiere a Zorro | archive-date=December 27, 2010 | date=December 10, 2010 | access-date= December 14, 2010 | work=[[Asistencia Asesoría y Administración]] | language=es}} In February 2011 the next title shot was awarded to [[Charly Manson]] to set up a grudge match between him and El Zorro, causing dissension between Park and Konnan. On February 28 Park entered the 2011 ''[[Rey de Reyes]]'' tournament in order to solidify his spot as the number one contender, defeating Dr. Wagner Jr., Halloween and [[Psicosis|Nicho el Millonario]] in his semifinal match.{{cite web | url= http://www.luchalibreaaa.com/elprofetahumillado.html | title= El Megacampeón, sangrado y humillado | date= March 1, 2011 | access-date= March 19, 2011 | work= [[Asistencia Asesoría y Administración]] | archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20110305024724/http://www.luchalibreaaa.com/elprofetahumillado.html | archive-date= March 5, 2011 | url-status= dead }} During the match Park was attacked by ''La Sociedad'' member Damián 666, who was seemingly trying to prevent him from advancing in the tournament, but instead the interference distracted Wagner Jr. and cost him the match. On March 18 at the [[Rey de Reyes (2011)|Rey de Reyes]] pay-per-view, Park was eliminated from the finals of the tournament, after brawling with rival El Mesías to a double countout.{{cite web | url= http://www.luchalibreaaa.com/reydereyes2011cronica.html | title= Solo uno dominó el Kaoz: Xtreme Tiger | date= March 18, 2011 | access-date= March 19, 2011 | work= [[Asistencia Asesoría y Administración]] | archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20110322182007/http://www.luchalibreaaa.com/reydereyes2011cronica.html | archive-date= March 22, 2011 | url-status= dead }} The following month, when El Zorro caught wind of Park's intention of challenging for his title, he seemingly started interfering in Park's matches under his old mask, costing him back–to–back multi–man tag team matches at the April 27 and 30 TV tapings, escalating the dissension within ''La Sociedad'', eventually leading to the group turning on El Zorro, after which it was revealed that the masked attacker had actually been Charly Manson and this had all been [[Cibernético]]'s plan to cause dissension within the ranks of ''La Sociedad''.{{cite web|url=http://www.wrestleview.com/viewnews.php?id=1304103120 |title=Viva La Raza! Lucha Weekly |author=Boutwell, Josh |date=April 29, 2011 |access-date=May 7, 2011 |work=WrestleView |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110513202607/http://www.wrestleview.com/viewnews.php?id=1304103120 |archive-date=May 13, 2011 }}{{cite web|url=http://www.wrestleview.com/viewnews.php?id=1304729572 |title=Viva La Raza! Lucha Weekly |author=Boutwell, Josh |date=May 6, 2011 |access-date=May 7, 2011 |work=WrestleView |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110514120631/http://www.wrestleview.com/viewnews.php?id=1304729572 |archive-date=May 14, 2011 }}{{cite web | url= http://superluchas.com/video-charly-manson-es-el-zorro-falso/ | title= Video: Charly Manson es el Zorro Falso | author= Ruiz Glez, Alex | date=June 7, 2011| access-date= June 7, 2011 | work=[[Súper Luchas]] Magazine | language=es}} On May 18, Park accepted El Mesías' challenge for a Mask vs. Hair match at [[Triplemanía XIX]].{{cite web|url=http://superluchas.com/de-ultimo-momento-la-park-vs-mesias-mascara-vs-cabellera-en-triplemania-19/ |title=De último momento: ¡¡¡LA Park vs Mesías, máscara vs cabellera en Triplemania 19!!! |author=Ruiz Glez, Alex |date=May 18, 2011 |access-date=May 19, 2011 |work=[[Súper Luchas]] Magazine |language=es |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110603032130/http://superluchas.com/2011/05/18/de-ultimo-momento-%C2%A1%C2%A1%C2%A1la-park-vs-mesias-mascara-vs-cabellera-en-triplemania-19/ |archive-date= June 3, 2011 |url-status=live }} Park added to the stakes of the match by announcing that he would retire, should he lose his mask.{{cite web | url= http://superluchas.com/la-park-asegura-que-si-pierde-la-mascara-ante-mesias-se-retira/ | title= LA Park asegura que si pierde la máscara ante El Mesías se retira | author= Ruiz Glez, Alex | date=May 23, 2011| access-date= June 1, 2011 | work=[[Súper Luchas]] Magazine | language=es}} On June 18 at Triplemanía XIX, Park defeated El Mesías, forcing him to have his head shaved.{{cite web|url=http://superluchas.com/triplemania-xix-cobertura-y-resultados-18-de-junio-de-2011-la-park-vs-el-mesias-mascara-vs-cabellera-tna-invade-triple-a/ |title=Triplemania XIX (Cobertura y resultados 18 de Junio de 2011) – LA Park vs El Mesias Mascara vs Cabellera, TNA invade Triple A |author=Cano Vela, Eduardo |date=June 17, 2011 |access-date=June 18, 2011 |work=[[Súper Luchas]] Magazine |language=es |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151016025256/http://superluchas.com/triplemania-xix-cobertura-y-resultados-18-de-junio-de-2011-la-park-vs-el-mesias-mascara-vs-cabellera-tna-invade-triple-a/ |archive-date=October 16, 2015 }} On July 31 at ''[[Verano de Escándalo (2011)|Verano de Escándalo]]'', Park faced ''La Sociedad'' stablemate and new AAA Mega Champion [[Jeff Jarrett]] and Dr. Wagner Jr. in a three-way match for the title, with Konnan stating that Park's job was to ensure that the title stayed with Jarrett.{{cite web | url=http://luchalibreaaa.com/%C2%A1l-a-park-por-fin-retador-al-titulo-maximo.php | title=¡L.A. Park, por fin retador al título máximo! | date=July 19, 2011 | access-date=August 1, 2011 | work=[[Asistencia Asesoría y Administración]] | language=es | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110722191435/http://luchalibreaaa.com/%C2%A1l-a-park-por-fin-retador-al-titulo-maximo.php | archive-date=July 22, 2011 | url-status=dead }} After Wagner Jr. was eliminated from the match, Jarrett pinned Park to retain his title, when someone masked as El Zorro interfered and hit him with a guitar.{{cite web | url= http://www.record.com.mx/luchalibre/2011-07-31/x-fly-fue-rapado-en-verano-de-escandalo-0 | title= X-Fly fue rapado en Verano de Escándalo | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20120615141634/http://www.record.com.mx/luchalibre/2011-07-31/x-fly-fue-rapado-en-verano-de-escandalo-0 | archive-date=June 15, 2012 | date=July 31, 2011 | access-date= August 1, 2011 | work=[[Récord (Mexican newspaper)|Récord]] | language=es}} This person was later revealed as ''La Sociedad'' member [[Chessman (wrestler)|Chessman]], whom Konnan had sent to interfere in the match in order to have Park go after El Zorro instead of continuing to chase his stablemate's title.{{cite web | url= https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5N-Y2qStsj8 |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211213/5N-Y2qStsj8 |archive-date=December 13, 2021 |url-status=live| title= Conversación Jeff Jarrett - Konnan Parte 1- | date=September 10, 2011 | access-date= September 12, 2011 | work=[[Asistencia Asesoría y Administración]] | publisher=[[YouTube]] | language=es}}{{cbignore}} On October 9 at [[Héroes Inmortales (2011)|Héroes Inmortales]], Park took part in the ''[[Copa Antonio Peña]]'' [[Professional wrestling match types#Gauntlet match|gauntlet match]]. After turning on Jeff Jarrett and eliminating him from the match, Park was once again attacked by a masked El Zorro, which led to [[Electroshock (wrestler)|Electroshock]] defeating him to win the match.{{cite web | url= http://superluchas.com/heroes-inmortales-cobertura-y-resultados-9-de-octubre-de-2011-mesias-vs-sting/ | title= AAA Héroes Inmortales (Cobertura y resultados 9 de Octubre de 2011) – Mesias y Sting empatan y unen sus fuerzas contra Konnan, Jarrett y sus aliados, Wagner gana pero Octagón y La Parka lo traicionan, los perros pierden las cabelleras | last=Cano Vela | first=Eduardo | date= October 9, 2011 | access-date= October 9, 2011 | work=[[Súper Luchas]] Magazine | language=es}} Héroes Inmortales also saw La Parka turning on AAA and joining ''La Sociedad'', which led to him and L.A. Park forming an unlikely tag team on December 1, when they defeated the team of Dr. Wagner Jr. and Electroshock in the main event.{{cite web | url= http://superluchas.com/aaa-resultados-1ro-de-dic-cibernetico-y-jack-evans-masacrados-triunfan-las-parkas/ | title= AAA (Resultados 1ro. de dic.): Cibernético y Jack Evans masacrados – Triunfan Las Parkas | last=Mexicool | first=Rey | date=December 2, 2011 | access-date=December 2, 2011 | work=[[Súper Luchas]] Magazine | language=es}} On December 16 at [[Guerra de Titanes (2011)|Guerra de Titanes]], Park defeated Dr. Wagner Jr. for the [[AAA Latin American Championship]].{{cite web | url= http://superluchas.com/aaa-guerra-de-titanes-2011-cobertura-y-resultados-16-de-diciembre-de-2011-la-park-vs-dr-wagner-por-el-campeonato-latinoamericano-aaa-figuras-de-tna-estaran-presentes-slguerradetitanes/ | title= AAA Guerra de Titanes 2011 (Cobertura y resultados 16 de diciembre de 2011) – La Park vence a Dr. Wagner y es el nuevo Campeón Latinoamericano AAA, Los luchadores del "Consejo" toman AAA / #SLGuerradeTitanes | last=Cano Vela | first=Eduardo | date= December 16, 2011 | access-date= December 16, 2011 | work=[[Súper Luchas]] Magazine | language=es}} The rivalry between Park and Jeff Jarrett continued on March 18, 2012, at ''[[Rey de Reyes (2012)|Rey de Reyes]]'', where Jarrett's interference eliminated Park from the ''Rey de Reyes'' tournament. During the main event of the evening, Park in turn cost Jarrett the AAA Mega Championship in his match against El Mesías.{{cite web | url= http://superluchas.com/aaa-rey-de-reyes-cobetura-y-resultados-18-de-marzo-de-2012-quien-ganara-el-torneo-rey-de-reyes-2012/ | title= AAA Rey de Reyes (Cobetura y Resultados 18 de marzo de 2012) – ¿Quien ganara el torneo Rey de Reyes 2012? | last=Cano Vela | first=Eduardo | date=March 18, 2012 | access-date=March 18, 2012 | work=[[Súper Luchas]] Magazine | language=es}} On April 30, Park officially quit ''La Sociedad'' and joined AAA to continue his rivalry with the Jarretts.{{cite web | url= http://superluchas.com/la-park-y-la-parka-se-unen-con-el-lic-roldan-para-enfrentar-a-jarrett-y-la-sociedad-crece-la-rivalidad-entre-la-familia-wagner-y-el-consejo/ | title= LA Park y La Parka se unen con el Lic. Electroshock won the match for his team by pinning Angle, forcing Dorian to have his head shaved bald. However, after the match, the ''rudos'' overpowered the ''technicos'' and shaved Joaquín bald.{{cite web | url = http://superluchas.com/triplemania-xx-el-dia-ha-llegado-cobertura-y-resultados-5-de-agosto-de-2012-mascara-vs-mascara-dr-wagner-vs-mascara-ano-2000-jr-kurt-angle-en-mexico/ | title = Triplemania XX "El día ha llegado" (Cobertura y resultados 5 de agosto de 2012) – Máscara vs máscara: Dr. Wagner vs Máscara Año 2000 Jr. – ¡Kurt Angle en México! | date=August 5, 2012 | access-date=August 5, 2012 | last=Cano Vela | first=Eduardo | publisher =[[Súper Luchas]] Magazine | language = es}} On April 23, 2013, L.A. Park announced that he had left AAA, citing his desire to be free.{{cite web | url=http://www.mediotiempo.com/mas-deportes/lucha-libre/noticias/2013/04/23/la-park-anuncio-su-salida-de-aaa | title=L.A. Park anunció su salida de AAA | author=Redacción | date=April 23, 2013 | access-date=May 1, 2013 | work=MedioTiempo | language=es | publisher=[[MSN]] | url-status=dead | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130430155918/http://www.mediotiempo.com/mas-deportes/lucha-libre/noticias/2013/04/23/la-park-anuncio-su-salida-de-aaa | archive-date=April 30, 2013 }} Even after his AAA exit he kept promoting the possibility of a ''Lucha de Apuestas'' match against Dr. Wagner Jr. possibly promoted by El Hijo del Santo's Todo X el Todos (TxT) promotion.{{cite web | url=https://kaiser-sports.blogspot.com/2013/04/santo-confirma-wagner-vs-la-park.html#more | title=Santo confirma Wagner vs LA Park | date=April 29, 2013 | access-date=May 1, 2013 | work=Kaiser Sports Mexico | language=es | first=Pablo | last=Lozano | archive-date=March 4, 2016 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304101141/http://kaiser-sports.blogspot.com/2013/04/santo-confirma-wagner-vs-la-park.html#more | url-status=dead }} On June 16, Park made an appearance for AAA at [[Triplemanía XXI]] to present [[Blue Demon Jr.]] with the AAA Latin American Championship belt and officially announce his departure from the promotion.{{cite web | url=http://www.mediotiempo.com/mas-deportes/lucha-libre/noticias/2013/06/16/triplemania-xxi-en-vivo-minuto-aminuto | title=Triplemania XXI ¡en vivo, minuto aminuto! | last=Valdés | first=Apolo | date=June 16, 2013 | access-date=June 21, 2013 | work=Medio Tiempo | language=es | publisher=[[MSN]]}} ===Returns to CMLL (2014, 2015, 2018–2019)=== [[File:L.A. Park in the ring during a show in Cuernavaca]] On October 31, 2014, during CMLL's [[CMLL Super Viernes (October 2014)#October 31, 2014|''Dia de los Muerte'' Super Viernes]] show L.A. Park returned to CMLL, accompanied by his son. He interrupted a fight between [[Diamante Azul]] and [[Thunder (luchador)|Thunder]] as he walked to the ring, then issued an open challenge to any CMLL wrestler. At the time no one took the challenge.{{cite web | url=http://www.mediotiempo.com/mas-deportes/lucha-libre/noticias/2014/11/01/reaparecio-l-a-park-en-el-cmll | title=Reapareció L. A. A. Park no formará parte del CMLL | date=November 6, 2014 | access-date=November 6, 2014 | last=Valdés | first=Apolo | work=MedioTiempo | publisher=[[MSN]] | language=es | url-status=dead | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141107173235/http://www.mediotiempo.com/mas-deportes/lucha-libre/noticias/2014/11/06/l-a-park-no-formara-parte-del-cmll | archive-date=November 7, 2014 }} On August 19, 2015, Park announced his return to CMLL.{{cite web | url=http://www.mediotiempo.com/mas-deportes/lucha-libre/noticias/2015/08/19/la-park-y-wagner-jr-regresan-al-cmll | title=L.A. On September 8, CMLL announced it had severed its ties with Park for the time being for "violating the rules of CMLL" by insulting the [[Arena México]] crowd.{{cite web | url=http://www.mediotiempo.com/mas-deportes/lucha-libre/noticias/2015/09/08/l-a-park-fuera-del-cmll-por-insultar-al-publico | title=L. A. Park fuera del CMLL por insultar al público | date=September 8, 2015 | access-date=September 10, 2015 | work=MedioTiempo | publisher=[[MSN]] | language=es}} ===Second return to AAA (2018)=== On June 5, 2018, L.A. Park was revealed as one of the surprise competitors in AAA's ''Poker de Ases'' ("Poker Aces") match at ''[[Triplemanía XXVI]]'', betting his mask against [[Psycho Clown]], [[El Hijo del Fantasma]] and [[Pentagón Jr]] in the headline match of the show. Park won the battle, winning the mask of Hijo del Fantasma. On July 21, 2018, at ''[[AAA vs. Elite]]'', L.A. Park teamed with [[Electroshock (wrestler)|Electroshock]] and [[Puma King]] as representatives of Liga Elite, defeating Team AAA ([[Psycho Clown]], [[El Hijo del Fantasma]] and [[Rey Wagner]]).{{cite magazine | url=https://superluchas.com/resultados-aaa-vs-elite-la-sorpresa-fue-puma-king/ | title=Resultados AAA vs. Elite; la sorpresa fue Puma King | first=Ernesto | last=Ocampo | date=July 23, 2018 | access-date=July 23, 2018 | magazine=[[Súper Luchas]]| language=es}} ===Major League Wrestling (2018–2022)=== In April 2018, L.A. Park was announced to be returning to MLW as a member of Promociones Dorado, led by [[Salina de la Renta]].Archived at [https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211205/KzJ8HCWPWN4 Ghostarchive]{{cbignore}} and the [https://web.archive.org/web/20190412212606/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KzJ8HCWPWN4 Wayback Machine]{{cbignore}}: {{cite web| url = https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KzJ8HCWPWN4| title = LA Park returns to MLW | website=[[YouTube]]}}{{cbignore}} Park then entered a feud with [[Pentagon Jr.]] and [[Rey Fénix]], defeating the former in a Mexican Death match at MLW War Games on September 6, 2018.{{Cite news|url=https://www.sescoops.com/mlw-war-games-results-9-6/|title=MLW War Games Results (9/6)|newspaper=Se Scoops |date=September 7, 2018}} He would continue to feud with the two, as well as other people such as [[Sami Callihan]] and [[Mance Warner]], before losing to Pentagon and Fenix in a match for the [[MLW World Tag Team Championship]] in November.{{Cite news|url=https://www.sescoops.com/mlw-fightland-road-results-11-8/|title=MLW Fightland Results (11/8)|newspaper=Se Scoops |date=November 9, 2018}} L.A. Park would then defeat Pentagon on April 4, 2019, at MLW Rise of the Renegades.{{Cite news|url=https://www.sescoops.com/spoilers-mlw-rise-of-the-renegades-results-4-4/|title=Spoilers: MLW Rise of the Renegades Results (4/4)|newspaper=Se Scoops |date=April 5, 2019}} Park would receive a push in early 2019, after winning the second MLW Battle Riot, earning a future title shot against the MLW World Heavyweight Champion.{{Cite web|url=https://www.f4wonline.com/indies/mlw-battle-riot-2-live-results-40-wrestlers-vie-world-title-shot-280936|title = MLW Battle Riot 2 live results: 40 wrestlers vie for a World title shot|date = April 5, 2019}} On September 15, 2019, Salina de la Renta announced that L.A. Park would be cashing in his Battle Riot title shot against [[Jacob Fatu]] at [[Saturday Night SuperFight]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.cagesideseats.com/2019/9/8/20855239/la-park-cashing-in-jacob-fatu-title-bout-at-mlw-first-ppv|title=LA Park cashing in to fight Jacob Fatu in title bout at MLW's first PPV|date=September 8, 2019}} On the January 13, 2021, episode of ''Fusion'', L.A. Park, along with his son, [[El Hijo de L.A. Park]], won the [[MLW World Tag Team Championship]], from [[Marshall and Ross Von Erich]], thanks to help from [[Tom Lawlor]]. On March 31, 2022, L.A. Park, along with family members L.A. Park Jr. and Hijo de LA Park, participated in an event during [[WrestleMania 38|Wrestlemania]] week. Following a match with Fatu and [[Alexander Hammerstone|Hammerstone]], L.A. Park and his family members allegedly went off script, attacking Hammerstone and Fatu with real punches and chair shots. MLW fired Los Parks the following day as a result of the alleged attack.{{Cite news |last=Sapp |first=Sean Ross |date=April 16, 2022 |title=Details Behind MLW Brawl That Led to Los Parks Being Fired |url=https://www.fightful.com/wrestling/details-behind-mlw-brawl-led-los-parks-being-fired/ |access-date=January 18, 2026 |work=Fightful}} == Personal life == [[File:Las_Parkas.jpg|thumb|Tapia working with his son, El Hijo de LA Park]] Tapia is part of an extended wrestling family that also includes his brother Eustacio Jiménez Ibarra, who wrestled as [[El Hijo de Cien Caras]] ("The son of [[Cien Caras]]") before his death on November 29, 2010, and his son who wrestles as [[El Hijo de L.A. Park]] ("The son of L.A. Park"). Three of Tapia's uncles are also wrestlers working under the ring names [[Super Parka]], Johnny Ibarra, and Desalmado. Super Parka's son, Tapia's cousin, wrestles for CMLL as [[Volador Jr.]]{{cite book | author= Madigan, Dan | title= Mondo Lucha a Go Go: the bizarre and honorable world of wild Mexican wrestling | publisher= HarperCollins Publishers | year= 2007 | chapter = A family affair | pages = 128–132 | isbn=978-0-06-085583-3}} In January 2019 L.A. Park introduced "L.A. Park Jr.", presented as a son who decided to follow in L.A. Park's footsteps and become a professional wrestler. He had worked under the ring name "Último Sadox" up until that point.{{cite web | author=+LuchaTB | language=es | access-date=January 28, 2019 | publisher=[[YouTube]] | date=January 27, 2019 | url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7TShqJoOtt0 |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211213/7TShqJoOtt0 |archive-date=December 13, 2021 |url-status=live| title=L.A. Park presenta a L.A. Park Jr.}}{{cbignore}} It is unclear if L.A. Park Jr. is related to Tapia or if it is a case of someone paying for the use of the name in the same vein as [[El Hijo de Cien Caras]] or [[El Hijo del Gladiador]], who paid for the use of the names. He also has a daughter, born December 13, 2005.{{cite web |title=Pagano & Omega win at TripleMania, CMLL gifts Bandido/Volador for Christmas, EDM curfew |url=https://thecubsfan.com/cmll/2020/12/14/pagano-omega-win-at-triplemania-cmll-gifts-bandido-volador-for-christmas-edm-curfew/ |website=LuchaBlog |access-date=22 June 2026}} == Championships and accomplishments == * '''Alianza Universal de Lucha Libre''' **Copa Universo (2015){{cite web | url = https://estrellasdelring.blogspot.com/2015/06/para-la-park-la-copa-universo-2015-en.html | title = Para L.A Park la Copa Universo 2015 en el 48 Aniversario de la Arena López Mateos. | author=Reyes Ruiz, Eduardo | work =Estrellas del Ring | access-date = June 14, 2015 | language = es}} **Copa Universo (2019) – with [[Alberto El Patrón]]{{Cite web|url=https://www.cagematch.net//?id=1&nr=233120|title=AULL 52.
