[[Gerudo]] {{small|(as Ganondorf)}} | occupation = | affiliation = | fighting_style = | weapon = | family = | spouse = | significant_other = | children = | relatives = | religion = | origin = [[Hyrule]] | nationality = }} {{Nihongo foot|'''Ganon'''|ガノン|Ganon|lead=yes|group=lower-alpha}} is a character and the main [[antagonist]] of [[Nintendo]]'s ''[[The Legend of Zelda]]'' video game series and franchise, as well as the final [[Boss (video games)|boss]] in many ''Zelda'' titles. In his [[humanoid]] [[Gerudo]] form, he is known as {{nihongo foot|'''Ganondorf'''.|ガノンドロフ|Ganondorofu|lead=yes|group=lower-alpha}} A massive and malevolent porcine monster, Ganon first appeared in the original ''[[The Legend of Zelda (video game)|The Legend of Zelda]]'' game in 1986, while his alter ego, Ganondorf, was introduced in ''[[The Legend of Zelda: A Link to the Past|A Link to the Past]]'' and made a physical appearance in ''[[Ocarina of Time]]''. He has since appeared in the majority of the games in the series in various forms. He is the [[archenemy]] of the protagonist [[Link (The Legend of Zelda)|Link]] and [[Princess Zelda]] of [[Universe of The Legend of Zelda#Hyrule|Hyrule]] and originally the leader of the Gerudo, a race of humanoid desert nomads before becoming the ruler of his demon army. His specific motives vary from game to game, but most often involve capturing Princess Zelda and planning to conquer Hyrule and the world at large. To this end, he seeks the [[Triforce]], an [[omnipotent]] artifact that grants any wish its bearer desires, and usually manipulates several other villains to realize his ambitions. In most games, he possesses the Triforce of Power, which gives him godlike strength, boundless mystical power, and invulnerability to all but the most powerful sacred weapons, such as the [[Master Sword]]. He appears in various spin-off games, such as ''[[Hyrule Warriors]]'' and ''[[Age of Calamity]]'', and the ''[[Super Smash Bros.]]'' series. The character has been well received by critics and is one of the most recognizable villains in gaming. The boss battles against Ganon have been praised as memorable and the character has been named as one of the greatest video game villains of all time. As the main villain of the series, Ganon has also appeared in a variety of media, including an [[The Legend of Zelda (animated series)|animated television series]] and [[manga]]. [[Uli Latukefu]] portrays Ganondorf in the [[The Legend of Zelda (film)|live-action film ''The Legend of Zelda'']].{{Cite magazine |url=https://deadline.com/2026/08/legend-of-zelda-uli-latukefu-ganondorf-1237027872/ |title=Uli Latukefu Lands Villain Role Of Ganondorf In Sony & Nintendo's 'The Legend Of Zelda' |last=Grobar |first=Matt |magazine=[[Deadline Hollywood]] |date=August 6, 2026 |access-date=August 6, 2026}} ==Concept and creation== Ganon was conceived as the antagonist of ''The Legend of Zelda'' video game by [[Shigeru Miyamoto]] working alongside [[Takashi Tezuka]].{{Cite magazine |last=Doyle |first=Patrick |date=2013-04-08 |title=Shigeru Miyamoto Shares Nintendo Secrets |url=https://www.rollingstone.com/culture/culture-lists/shigeru-miyamoto-shares-nintendo-secrets-19215/ |access-date=2023-07-23 |magazine=Rolling Stone |language=en-US |archive-date=2023-07-23 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230723103212/https://www.rollingstone.com/culture/culture-lists/shigeru-miyamoto-shares-nintendo-secrets-19215/ |url-status=live}} ===Characterisation=== [[File:Ganon (Oracle of Ages & Oracle of Seasons).png|thumb|left|upright=1|alt=Artwork of Ganon in his blue pig-like form |Ganon, as depicted in promotional artwork for [[The Legend of Zelda: Oracle of Ages and Oracle of Seasons|''The Legend of Zelda: Oracle of Ages'' and ''Oracle of Seasons'']]]] Ganon has two basic forms that appear throughout the series: one is a gigantic porcine form and the other is his humanoid Gerudo form. In the original ''The Legend of Zelda'', ''[[A Link to the Past]]'', [[The Legend of Zelda: Oracle of Seasons and Oracle of Ages|''Oracle of Seasons'' and ''Oracle of Ages'']], ''[[Four Swords Adventures]]'', ''[[A Link Between Worlds]]'', and ''[[Echoes of Wisdom]]'' he is depicted as a blue, bipedal [[pig]] wielding either a large sword or a trident. ''[[Ocarina of Time]]'' marks the first appearance of his humanoid form named Ganondorf, the physically imposing and armor-clad king of the Gerudo.{{Cite web |last=Norman |first=Jim |date=2023-04-20 |title=Are Ganondorf And Ganon The Same Person? - Zelda Villains Explained |url=https://www.nintendolife.com/guides/are-ganondorf-and-ganon-the-same-person-zelda-villains-explained |access-date=2023-07-28 |website=Nintendo Life |language=en-GB |archive-date=2023-07-28 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230728045847/https://www.nintendolife.com/guides/are-ganondorf-and-ganon-the-same-person-zelda-villains-explained |url-status=live}} For the development of ''Ocarina of Time'', Ganon was designed by character designer Satoru Takizawa. He imagined Ganon as a "crooked and complex thief, who was basically an all-around abominable human being". However, script director Toru Osawa thought that Ganondorf should have "parts where he is rather good", comparing him to the character of [[Raoh]] in ''[[Fist of the North Star]]''. With this idea in mind, Takizawa created a tentative model of Ganondorf based on actor [[Christopher Lambert]] (while the resulting designs were very different). Since Ganon had appeared earlier as a boar-like creature, Takizawa decided that Ganondorf should transform into such at the end of the game and wanted to consult Shigeru Miyamoto on this, but realised that he had no opinion on the matter. He decided on making Ganon a beast "with the feeling of a pig" to reference ''A Link to the Past''.{{Cite web |script-title=ja:ほぼ日刊イトイ新聞 - 樹の上の秘密基地 |url=https://www.1101.com/nintendo/nin1/nin1-6.htm |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231111090617/https://www.1101.com/nintendo/nin1/nin1-6.htm |archive-date=2023-11-11 |access-date=2023-08-30 |website=1101}} Following the release of ''[[Tears of the Kingdom]]'', the game's director [[Hidemaro Fujibayashi]] said that he had approached Ganondorf as a main character due to his long history in the series. He added that he considered Ganondorf to be the perfect opposing character to Princess Zelda due to being a king of the Gerudo with his own motivations. Series producer [[Eiji Aonuma]] said that although Ganondorf had been portrayed throughout the series as an evil character, ''Tears of the Kingdom'' was the first game to firmly establish him as overwhelmingly evil by including a violent scene where he kills another character.{{Cite web |date=2023-10-26 |title=革命の、その先の冒険。『ゼルダの伝説 ティアーズ オブ ザ キングダム』 開発者インタビュー – ページ 3 |url=https://www.ndw.jp/totk-interview-231026/3/ |access-date=2023-11-26 |website=Nintendo DREAM WEB |language=ja |archive-date=2023-11-26 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231126094918/https://www.ndw.jp/totk-interview-231026/3/ |url-status=live}} ===Names=== Ganon was originally known as "Hakkai" during development of the original ''The Legend of Zelda'', in reference to a humanoid pig character known as [[Zhu Bajie]] (''Cho Hakkai'' in Japanese) from the 16th century Chinese novel ''[[Journey to the West]]''.{{Cite web |title=Iwata Asks - Volume 2: The History of Handheld The Legend of Zelda Games - Page 5 |url=https://iwataasks.nintendo.com/interviews/ds/zelda/1/4/ |access-date=2023-07-23 |website=iwataasks.nintendo.com |language=en |archive-date=2023-08-30 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230830163711/https://iwataasks.nintendo.com/interviews/ds/zelda/1/4/ |url-status=live}} The character was given the name "Ganondorf Dragmire" in the English version of the ''[[The Legend of Zelda: A Link to the Past|A Link to the Past]]'' instruction manual while his monster form's name was "Mandrag Ganon".{{cite book|author=Yoshiaki Koizumi|url=https://www.nintendo.co.jp/clvs/manuals/common/pdf/CLV-P-SAAEE.pdf|title=Instruction Booklet (for ''The Legend of Zelda: A Link to the Past'')|date=1992|publisher=Nintendo of America|page=5|section=The Legend of Hyrule|quote=The name of this king of thieves is Ganondorf Dragmire, but he is known by his alias, Mandrag Ganon, which means Ganon of the Enchanted Thieves.|access-date=2020-06-18|archive-date=2020-11-11|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201111203355/https://www.nintendo.co.jp/clvs/manuals/common/pdf/CLV-P-SAAEE.pdf|url-status=live}} In 2017, Nintendo reconfirmed that "Dragmire" is the character's surname on its official Zelda website.{{Cite web|last=Phillips|first=Tom|date=2017-04-20|title=Nintendo's official Zelda site states Ganondorf surname|url=https://www.eurogamer.net/articles/2017-04-20-nintendos-official-zelda-site-states-ganondorf-surname|access-date=2021-12-03|website=Eurogamer|language=en|archive-date=2021-12-03|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211203150333/https://www.eurogamer.net/articles/2017-04-20-nintendos-official-zelda-site-states-ganondorf-surname|url-status=live}} Ganon was sometimes spelled inconsistently in earlier games. In the Japanese versions of the first three games, his name is anglicized as "Gannon".{{cite video game|title=[[The Legend of Zelda (video game)|The Hyrule Fantasy: Zelda no Densetsu]]|developer=[[Nintendo Entertainment Analysis and Development]]|publisher=[[Nintendo]]|date=1986-02-21|platform=[[Family Computer Disk System]]|scene=title screen|quote=Many years ago prince darkness Gannon stole one of the Triforce with power.}}{{cite video game|title=[[Zelda II: The Adventure of Link|The Legend of Zelda 2: Link no Bōken]]|developer=[[Nintendo Entertainment Analysis and Development]]|publisher=[[Nintendo]]|date=1987-01-14|platform=[[Family Computer Disk System]]|scene=title screen|quote=Several years after Gannon was destroyed, Link learns from Impa about another sleeping Princess Zelda.}}{{cite video game|title=[[The Legend of Zelda: A Link to the Past|Zelda no Densetsu: Kamigami no Triforce]]|developer=[[Nintendo Entertainment Analysis and Development]]|publisher=[[Nintendo]]|date=1991-11-21|platform=[[Super Famicom]]|scene=staff credits|quote=Level 8 Gannon's Tower}} This spelling appears in two Western releases: the original ''The Legend of Zelda'', and the non-canonical ''[[Zelda's Adventure]]''.{{Cite web |last=Schneider |first=Peer |date=2002-01-26 |title=Hyrule Times Vol. 13: Zelda's Adventure |url=https://www.ign.com/articles/2002/01/26/hyrule-times-vol-13-zeldas-adventure |access-date=2023-07-28 |website=IGN |language=en |archive-date=2023-05-12 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230512195654/https://www.ign.com/articles/2002/01/26/hyrule-times-vol-13-zeldas-adventure |url-status=live}} ===Character design=== Like all Gerudo, Ganondorf possesses olive dark skin, amber eyes, and red hair. Ganondorf is around {{convert|230|cm|ftin}} and was first drawn with a "sharp, birdlike nose" that is characteristic of the Gerudo and "strong, supple muscles".{{Cite book|title=Hyrule Historia|publisher=Dark Horse Books|year=2013|page=148}} Ganondorf's clothing in ''Ocarina of Time'' was designed in the style of a 1980s [[visual kei]] band, with producer Toru Osawa suggesting that his design incorporate a color scheme of red, black, and gold.{{cite web |url=https://www.1101.com/nintendo/nin1/nin1-13.htm |title=ほぼ日刊イトイ新聞 - 樹の上の秘密基地 |work=1101 |date=December 10, 1998 |access-date=January 22, 2024 |archive-date=July 8, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220708071040/https://www.1101.com/nintendo/nin1/nin1-13.htm |url-status=live}} In ''[[The Wind Waker]]'', Ganondorf was designed as an older version of his ''Ocarina of Time'' incarnation. The artists depicted him as middle-aged and created drawings of him "with an Eastern flavor". His robe was decorated with patterns that were designed to be a twist on the mark of the Gerudo seen previously.{{Cite book|title=Hyrule Historia|publisher=Dark Horse Books|year=2013|page=156}} Ganondorf's reappearance in ''[[Twilight Princess]]'' returned him to a similar age to his original appearance in ''Ocarina of Time''. His design was created to look like a warrior, dressed in armour. He also transforms into Demonic Beast Ganon and this concept art was created with the caption "Pig Ganon".{{Cite book|title=Hyrule Historia|publisher=Dark Horse Books|year=2013|pages=176–177, 232}} Ganon evolved into other monstrous forms for his appearance in ''[[Breath of the Wild]]''. He is presented as a primal evil force that is visible as a serpentine cloud circling around Hyrule Castle.{{Cite web |last=Mejia |first=Ozzie |date=2023-05-11 |title=A brief history of Ganon, The Legend of Zelda's greatest villain |url=https://www.shacknews.com/article/135439/legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom-ganon-history |access-date=2023-07-23 |website=Shacknews |language=en |archive-date=2023-07-23 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230723072618/https://www.shacknews.com/article/135439/legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom-ganon-history |url-status=live}} His physical form Calamity Ganon is a grotesque monster that resembles a spider equipped with various weapons. His final form is Dark Beast Ganon, a giant boar similar to previous iterations. Artist Yuki Hamada explained that his enormous size was due to the team wanting the game to end in the vast open plain of Hyrule Field. In addition, the Blight Ganons that Link encounters in the Divine Beasts were designed with similar design features, such as his red hair, as the artist Takafumi Kiuchi wanted players to feel Ganon's presence at all times.{{Cite book|title=The Legend of Zelda Breath of the Wild: Creating a Champion|publisher=Dark Horse Books|year=2017|pages=75–81}} For the return of Ganondorf in ''[[Tears of the Kingdom]]'' the character's design was reassigned to Takizawa. Fujibayashi said that he had given him the task of making him a "very cool, very awesome [[Mazoku|demon king]]" due to him being a crucial character within the series.{{Cite web |last=Pulliam-Moore |first=Charles |date=2023-05-12 |title=A conversation with The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom's creative leads |url=https://www.theverge.com/23721063/zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom-interview-aonuma-fujibayashi |access-date=2023-05-20 |website=The Verge |language=en-US |archive-date=2023-05-12 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230512171338/https://www.theverge.com/23721063/zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom-interview-aonuma-fujibayashi |url-status=live}} He said that the designer intended to give Ganondorf an evil appearance but also wanted him to appear good so that anyone could fall in love with him. The team spent time designing his facial expressions to give him brutality but also a sense of humanity. Ganondorf's appearance was designed with the flavour of a Japanese warlord. Every aspect of his design was carefully considered to give the impression of strength, elegance and intelligence and to portray a character with fine tastes who takes care of his appearance. ===Portrayal=== [[File:Matthew Mercer by Gage Skidmore.jpg|thumb|upright=.75|alt=Headshot of Matthew Mercer |[[Matthew Mercer]] provides Ganondorf's English voice in ''[[The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom]]''.]] Ganon has been voiced by several voice actors. In the 1989 ''[[The Legend of Zelda (Television Series)|The Legend of Zelda]]'' animated television series and ''[[Captain N: The Game Master]]'', he was voiced by [[Len Carlson]].{{Cite web |title=Len CARLSON - Anime News Network |url=https://www.animenewsnetwork.com/encyclopedia/people.php?id=6738 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230822013734/https://www.animenewsnetwork.com/encyclopedia/people.php?id=6738 |archive-date=22 August 2023 |access-date=2023-08-30 |website=www.animenewsnetwork.com}} In the ''Zelda'' series and other spin-off games, the character has been voiced by several Japanese voice actors, including [[Takashi Nagasako]] in ''[[Ocarina of Time]]'', ''[[The Wind Waker]]'', ''[[Super Smash Bros. Melee]]'' and ''[[Super Smash Bros. Ultimate|Ultimate]]''; [[Hironori Miyata]] in ''[[The Legend of Zelda: Twilight Princess|Twilight Princess]]'', ''[[Super Smash Bros. Brawl]]'' and ''[[Super Smash Bros. for Nintendo 3DS and Wii U]]''; [[Taiten Kusunoki]] in ''[[Hyrule Warriors]]''; and Kōsuke Takaguchi in ''[[Tears of the Kingdom]]''.{{Cite web|title=Ganon Voices (Legend of Zelda)|url=https://www.behindthevoiceactors.com/characters/The-Legend-of-Zelda/Ganon/|access-date=2021-12-09|website=Behind The Voice Actors|language=en-US|archive-date=2021-12-23|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211223222634/https://www.behindthevoiceactors.com/characters/The-Legend-of-Zelda/Ganon/|url-status=live}} In the English dub of ''[[Tears of the Kingdom]]'', he is voiced by [[Matthew Mercer]], who unofficially portrayed the character in the [[live action]] web series ''There Will Be Brawl''. He will be portrayed by [[Uli Latukefu]] in the [[The Legend of Zelda (film)|live-action ''Legend of Zelda'' movie]].{{Cite web |last=Grobar |first=Matt |date=2026-08-06 |title='Legend Of Zelda': Uli Latukefu Set For Ganondorf Role |url=https://deadline.com/2026/08/legend-of-zelda-uli-latukefu-ganondorf-1237027872/ |access-date=2026-08-06 |website=Deadline |language=en-US}} ==Characteristics== Ganon is the main antagonist in ''The Legend of Zelda'' series. He usually appears as the final boss at the end of each game. A recurring storyline in the series centres around the protagonist Link fighting to save Princess Zelda after she is captured by Ganon. Over the course of the series, Ganon has been depicted in various physical forms. His humanoid form known as Ganondorf is the king and only male member of the Gerudo, a race predominantly consisting of female warriors.{{Cite magazine |last=Reeves |first=Ben |date=9 August 2012 |title=The Evolution Of Ganon |url=https://www.gameinformer.com/b/features/archive/2012/08/09/the-evolution-of-ganon.aspx |access-date=2023-07-23 |magazine=Game Informer |language=en |archive-date=2020-11-12 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201112011110/https://www.gameinformer.com/b/features/archive/2012/08/09/the-evolution-of-ganon.aspx |url-status=live}} His monstrous bestial form, Ganon, resembles a giant boar. In some games, either Ganon or Ganondorf appear as the final boss, whereas in others, he transforms between the two.{{Cite web |last=Diaz |first=Ana |date=2023-04-18 |title=The difference between Ganon and Ganondorf, explained |url=https://www.polygon.com/23688032/ganon-vs-ganondorf-explained-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom |access-date=2023-07-29 |website=Polygon |language=en-US |archive-date=2023-07-31 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230731003319/https://www.polygon.com/23688032/ganon-vs-ganondorf-explained-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom |url-status=live}} Throughout the series, Ganon has been characterised as the embodiment of evil and is placed in direct opposition to the protagonist Link and Princess Zelda across multiple generations in the fictional timeline. In ''[[Skyward Sword]]'', he is implied to be the manifestation of the antagonist [[Demon King Demise]]'s hatred following the character's defeat.{{Cite web |last=Cryer |first=Hirun |date=2023-04-14 |title=Is Demise back in The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom? It's complicated |url=https://www.gamesradar.com/is-demise-back-in-the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom-its-complicated/ |access-date=2023-07-24 |website=GamesRadar+ |language=en |archive-date=2023-07-13 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230713221052/https://www.gamesradar.com/is-demise-back-in-the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom-its-complicated/ |url-status=live}} The game was presented as the start of [[The Legend of Zelda Timeline|''The Legend of Zelda'' fictional timeline]] and the origin of his endless battle with Link and Zelda.{{Cite web |last=Parkin |first=Jeffrey |date=2023-03-08 |title=The Zelda timeline doesn't matter |url=https://www.polygon.com/zelda/23618364/zelda-timeline-tears-of-the-kingdom-hero-zelda-link-ganon-myth-breath-wild-sequel |access-date=2023-07-30 |website=Polygon |language=en-US |archive-date=2023-07-30 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230730080004/https://www.polygon.com/zelda/23618364/zelda-timeline-tears-of-the-kingdom-hero-zelda-link-ganon-myth-breath-wild-sequel |url-status=live}} In ''Breath of the Wild'', his Dark Beast Ganon form is described as "Hatred and Malice Incarnate". The character's motivations typically centre around destroying Hyrule or placing himself in a position of power as ruler. His destructive influence is illustrated in ''Ocarina of Time'', when Link awakens from a seven-year sleep to discover Hyrule transformed from a peaceful kingdom to a place of fear shrouded in darkness following Ganondorf's rise to power.{{Cite web|last=Gratton|first=Kyle|date=2021-04-06|title=Ocarina of Time Shows Ganon's Power Better Than Any Other Zelda Game|url=https://screenrant.com/zelda-ganon-power-ocarina-time-hyrule-change-differences/|url-status=live|access-date=2021-12-26|website=ScreenRant|language=en-US|archive-date=2021-12-26|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211226001726/https://screenrant.com/zelda-ganon-power-ocarina-time-hyrule-change-differences/}} In ''Breath of the Wild'', his destructive power is so great, that he almost wipes out the entire civilisation of Hyrule in a cataclysm known as the Great Calamity. In the fictional lore of the series, Ganon is the bearer of the Triforce of Power, one of three components that form a core symbol of the series, a divine relic called the [[Triforce]]. The three pieces of the Triforce represent the qualities of the three characters, with Ganon being the bearer of the Triforce of Power and Link and Zelda bearing the Triforce of Courage and Wisdom respectively.{{Cite web |last=Plunkett |first=Luke |date=2011-07-21 |title=The Real History of the Triforce |url=https://kotaku.com/the-real-history-of-the-triforce-5823249 |access-date=2023-07-29 |website=Kotaku |language=en |archive-date=2023-08-30 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230830164227/https://kotaku.com/the-real-history-of-the-triforce-5823249 |url-status=live}} A recurring plot element in the series is Ganon's desire to obtain the completed Triforce, which offers limitless power to its bearer. This struggle for control of the Triforce has been a central aspect of several games, such as ''Ocarina of Time'', and binds the three main characters in an eternal battle across the fictional ''Zelda'' timeline.{{Cite web|last=Hogeweg|first=Stan|date=2021-08-11|title=Zelda: Breath of the Wild 2 Should Bring Back One Feature the First Game Skipped|url=https://gamerant.com/zelda-breath-of-the-wild-2-triforce-link-ganon/|url-status=live|access-date=2021-12-27|website=Game Rant|language=en-US|archive-date=2021-12-27|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211227073947/https://gamerant.com/zelda-breath-of-the-wild-2-triforce-link-ganon/}} ===Powers and abilities=== Ganon/Ganondorf is presented as a dangerous foe who is difficult to defeat. He is a formidable warrior and [[Magician (fantasy)|sorcerer]], capable of [[dual-wielding]] large blades, such as [[great sword]]s.{{Cite web|date=2018-09-06|title=Legend Of Zelda: 15 Superpowers Fans Forgot Ganon Has (And 15 He Never Uses)|url=https://www.thegamer.com/legend-zelda-15-superpowers-fans-forgot-ganon-15-never-uses/|access-date=2021-12-07|website=TheGamer|language=en-US|archive-date=2021-12-09|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211209194913/https://www.thegamer.com/legend-zelda-15-superpowers-fans-forgot-ganon-15-never-uses/|url-status=live}} He is typically only defeated by Link with the use of a legendary weapon like the [[Master Sword]] or Light Arrows. Due to his near-immortality and indestructible power, he often needs to be sealed away in another realm by magic to prevent him from causing more destruction. Like Link and Zelda, he is repeatedly [[Reincarnation|reincarnated]] in subsequent games.{{Cite web |last=Castello |first=Jay |date=2023-07-22 |title=Tears of the Kingdom's ending is its own kind of tragedy |url=https://www.polygon.com/legend-zelda-tears-kingdom/23802993/loz-totk-ending-zelda-dragon-master-sword-ganondorf |access-date=2023-07-23 |website=Polygon |language=en-US |archive-date=2023-07-23 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230723015844/https://www.polygon.com/legend-zelda-tears-kingdom/23802993/loz-totk-ending-zelda-dragon-master-sword-ganondorf |url-status=live}} In addition to his combat skills, he also demonstrates various magical powers that originate in his use of [[dark magic]]. He can use various defensive measures in combat, such as creating magical barriers.{{Cite web|date=2018-10-23|title=The Legend Of Zelda: 20 Superpowers Ganondorf Has That Are Kept Hidden|url=https://www.thegamer.com/legend-of-zelda-ganondorf-abilities/|access-date=2021-12-07|website=TheGamer|language=en-US|archive-date=2021-12-08|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211208110857/https://www.thegamer.com/legend-of-zelda-ganondorf-abilities/|url-status=live}} In the original ''The Legend of Zelda'' game and ''A Link to the Past'' he is able to turn himself invisible. Ganondorf also has the ability of teleportation, giving him the advantage of sneaking behind his opponent in combat, a skill that he displays in ''Twilight Princess''. In ''Ocarina of Time'' he has the ability to [[Levitation (paranormal)|levitate]]. He has also demonstrated that he can pass between dimensions, such as the Dark World and the Twilight Realm. In several games, he is able to create a mini boss in his own likeness named Phantom Ganon. In ''Ocarina of Time'', Phantom Ganon is the boss of the Forest Temple and appears as a ghostly rider that can jump in and out of paintings.{{Cite web |last=Sliva |first=Marty |date=2023-05-01 |title=Ocarina of Time's Forest Temple Is Zelda Dungeon Perfection |url=https://www.escapistmagazine.com/ocarina-of-time-forest-temple-is-zelda-dungeon-perfection/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230501214228/https://www.escapistmagazine.com/ocarina-of-time-forest-temple-is-zelda-dungeon-perfection/ |archive-date=1 May 2023 |access-date=2023-08-31 |website=The Escapist |language=en-US}} In ''The Wind Waker'', he creates Puppet Ganon, a [[marionette]] that takes three forms, each requiring a different strategy to defeat.{{Cite web |last=Gray |first=Kate |date=2023-06-25 |title=The 15 Best Zelda Bosses, Ranked |url=https://www.nintendolife.com/features/the-15-best-zelda-bosses-ranked |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230108140026/https://www.nintendolife.com/features/the-15-best-zelda-bosses-ranked |archive-date=8 January 2023 |access-date=2023-08-31 |website=Nintendo Life |language=en-GB}} In ''Tears of the Kingdom'', Phantom Ganon is a powerful foe that deals additional damage with an expanding pool of gloom.{{Cite web |last=Ostler |first=Anne-Marie |date=2023-07-17 |title=300 hours in, Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom player makes horrifying Phantom Ganon discovery |url=https://www.gamesradar.com/300-hours-in-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom-player-makes-horrifying-phantom-ganon-discovery/ |access-date=2023-07-23 |website=GamesRadar+ |language=en |archive-date=2023-07-23 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230723180323/https://www.gamesradar.com/300-hours-in-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom-player-makes-horrifying-phantom-ganon-discovery/ |url-status=live}} He also has the power to possess and control other characters. In ''Twilight Princess'' he possesses Princess Zelda and uses her body like a puppet to fight Link. He can also manipulate other characters for his own benefit, such as [[Zant]] in ''Twilight Princess''. In ''Breath of the Wild'', Calamity Ganon is able to corrupt creatures with the spread of a substance called Malice.{{Cite web |date=2022-09-21 |title=The Legend of Zelda: What is Malice? |url=https://gamerant.com/the-legend-of-zelda-malice-lore-story-purpose-explained/ |access-date=2023-07-23 |website=Game Rant |language=en |archive-date=2023-07-23 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230723181033/https://gamerant.com/the-legend-of-zelda-malice-lore-story-purpose-explained/ |url-status=live}} He reinstates his influence over the land of Hyrule in ''Breath of the Wild'' and ''Tears of the Kingdom'' by conjuring a Blood Moon, which resurrects fallen monsters.{{Cite web |last=Bunce |first=Nic |date=2023-05-22 |title=What is the Blood Moon in Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom? |url=https://www.polygon.com/zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom-guide/23732914/blood-moon-length-cooking |access-date=2023-07-23 |website=Polygon |language=en-US |archive-date=2023-07-22 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230722093048/https://www.polygon.com/zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom-guide/23732914/blood-moon-length-cooking |url-status=live}}{{Cite news |date=2023-06-02 |title=Zelda Tears of the Kingdom Blood Moon effects, timing and cooking bonus |language=en |work=Eurogamer.net |url=https://www.eurogamer.net/zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom-blood-moon-effects-timing-cooking-bonus-9343 |access-date=2023-07-23 |archive-date=2023-07-23 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230723183753/https://www.eurogamer.net/zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom-blood-moon-effects-timing-cooking-bonus-9343 |url-status=live}} ==Appearances== ===''The Legend of Zelda'' series=== [[File:Ganon screenshot 1986.jpg|thumb|right|upright=1|alt=Screenshot of ''The Legend of Zelda'' video game featuring Ganon and Link |Ganon's first appearance in the original 1986 ''[[The Legend of Zelda (video game)|The Legend of Zelda]]'']] Ganon made his first appearance in the original [[NES]] video game ''[[The Legend of Zelda (video game)|The Legend of Zelda]]'' in 1986 in the form of a blue monstrous pig. The game established the character's desire for power, which was reiterated in subsequent games. The storyline involves Ganon invading Hyrule with his army and stealing the Triforce of Power. To prevent him from obtaining the Triforce of Wisdom, Princess Zelda scatters the eight pieces across the kingdom. Link is then sent on a quest to retrieve the eight fragments and finally defeats Ganon using a silver arrow.{{Cite web|last=Schedeen|first=Jesse|date=15 June 2010|title=Big Boss of the Day: Ganondorf|url=https://www.ign.com/articles/2010/06/15/big-boss-of-the-day-ganondorf|url-status=live|access-date=4 December 2021|website=IGN|archive-date=4 December 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211204121003/https://www.ign.com/articles/2010/06/15/big-boss-of-the-day-ganondorf}} The second entry in the ''Zelda'' series, which is titled ''[[Zelda II: The Adventure of Link]]'', does not feature the physical presence of Ganon, but his image appears in the final [[game over]] screen, signifying his return.{{Cite web|last=Heath|first=Thomas|date=2021-07-07|title=Legend Of Zelda: Every Version Of Ganon Ranked By Power|url=https://www.thegamer.com/legend-zelda-ganon-versions-ranked-power/|url-status=live|access-date=2021-12-05|website=TheGamer|language=en-US|archive-date=2022-05-29|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220529193921/http://www.thegamer.com/legend-zelda-ganon-versions-ranked-power/}} He was reintroduced in the [[Super Nintendo Entertainment System]] game ''[[A Link to the Past]]''. It expands on Ganon's backstory by revealing that he used to be a man named Ganondorf, the leader of a group of thieves, who enters the Sacred Realm and steals the Triforce, which plunges the Sacred Realm into darkness. After he is sealed in the Dark World, Link and Zelda are sent there by the wizard Agahnim, who is an avatar used to contain Ganon's spirit. Once Link defeats Agahnim in the Dark World, Ganon rises from his body and turns into a bat. He is finally defeated by Link at the Pyramid of Power.{{Cite web |date=2021-01-27 |title=Zelda: Every Time Ganon Tried To Take Over Hyrule, Explained |url=https://screenrant.com/zelda-ganon-link-save-hyrule-evil-all-games/ |access-date=2021-12-30 |website=ScreenRant |language=en-US |archive-date=2021-12-30 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211230093838/https://screenrant.com/zelda-ganon-link-save-hyrule-evil-all-games/ |url-status=live}} In ''[[Link's Awakening]]'', the fourth Shadow Nightmare that Link faces in the final boss battle is based on Ganon from ''A Link to the Past''.{{Cite web |last=Baird |first=Scott |date=2020-01-14 |title=The Legend of Zelda: Link's Awakening - How to Defeat the Shadow Nightmare Boss |url=https://screenrant.com/the-legend-of-zelda-links-awakening-how-to-defeat-the-shadow-nightmare-boss/ |access-date=2022-01-26 |website=ScreenRant |language=en-US |archive-date=2022-01-26 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220126234206/https://screenrant.com/the-legend-of-zelda-links-awakening-how-to-defeat-the-shadow-nightmare-boss/ |url-status=live}} ''[[Ocarina of Time]]'', which was released for the [[Nintendo 64]], introduced the character in his humanoid form as Ganondorf, the king of the Gerudo thieves, expanding upon the backstory in ''A Link to the Past''. Ganondorf schemes to take the Triforce from the Sacred Realm in order to conquer Hyrule and, after a young Link is put in a seven-year sleep, Link wakes as an adult to discover that Ganondorf is now ruling over Hyrule. After stealing the Triforce, Ganondorf's evil heart breaks it into three pieces, with Ganondorf keeping the Triforce of Power. In the final boss fight, Link and Ganondorf battle at Ganon's Castle, but before the fight is over, he transforms into his beast form, Ganon. He is finally defeated by Link and sealed in the Dark Realm. In 2001, two games titled [[Oracle of Seasons and Oracle of Ages|''Oracle of Seasons'' and ''Oracle of Ages'']] were released for the [[Game Boy Color]] handheld console. They feature their own antagonists, but upon completing either game, the player receives a password that provides access to a linked game in the opposite title. The linked game reveals Ganon as the secret final boss, who was resurrected by two witches named [[Twinrova]]. Ganondorf resumes his plans to obtain the Triforce and conquer Hyrule in ''[[The Wind Waker]]''. Although he is not initially presented as the main villain, he is revealed to be the master of the Helmaroc King. He kidnaps multiple young girls with pointed ears in order to find Zelda so he can complete the Triforce and take over Hyrule, including Link's younger sister Aryll.{{Cite web |last=Alexander |first=Cristina |date=2023-06-12 |title=How to Play The Legend of Zelda Games in Chronological Order |url=https://www.ign.com/articles/the-legend-of-zelda-games-in-order |access-date=2023-07-30 |website=IGN |language=en |archive-date=2023-07-30 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230730144902/https://www.ign.com/articles/the-legend-of-zelda-games-in-order |url-status=live}} In the final boss battle, Link defeats him by thrusting the Master Sword into his forehead, turning him to stone.{{Cite web |last=Plunkett |first=Luke |date=2020-05-06 |title=Wind Waker's Ending Was Incredibly Badass |url=https://kotaku.com/wind-wakers-ending-was-incredibly-badass-1843171401 |access-date=2023-07-30 |website=Kotaku |language=en |archive-date=2023-05-13 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230513070424/https://kotaku.com/wind-wakers-ending-was-incredibly-badass-1843171401 |url-status=live}} In ''[[Four Swords Adventures]]'', the antagonists are initially shown to be Shadow Link and Vaati. However, Ganon is revealed to be the true villain who stole a powerful magical trident and Dark Mirror to create the evil version of Link. Ganon uses Shadow Link to kidnap the shrine maidens of Hyrule and murders the Knights of Hyrule, trapping them in the World of Darkness. Link and his clones free the shrine maidens and seal Ganon inside the Four Sword to return peace to Hyrule. In ''[[Twilight Princess]]'', Ganondorf manipulates the sorcerer Zant to usurp the throne of the Twilight Realm. In the game's backstory, the Sages banish Ganon with the Mirror of Twilight for trying to steal the Triforce. After Link and his companion Midna defeat Zant, they face Ganondorf for the final battle at Hyrule Castle. Ganondorf battles Link by possessing Zelda and using her like a puppet and afterwards transforms into his beast form. After Link slays Ganon, Midna safely transports Link and Zelda to Hyrule field, but Link is forced to again face Ganondorf in his humanoid form. Ganondorf is defeated with the help of Zelda's Light Arrows when Link finally plunges the Master Sword into Ganondorf's chest. Ganon was replaced by two new antagonists named [[Ghirahim]] and [[Demon King Demise]] in ''[[Skyward Sword]]''. Speaking to ''[[Nintendo Power]]'', [[Eiji Aonuma]] explained that he wanted a different kind of villain and that Ghirahim was created to contrast with Ganon's "very masculine, powerful, evil" image.{{Cite web|last=Phillips|first=Tom|date=2011-07-25|title=Ganon not in Zelda: Skyward Sword|url=https://www.eurogamer.net/articles/2011-07-25-ganon-not-in-zelda-skyward-sword|access-date=2021-12-04|website=Eurogamer|language=en|archive-date=2021-12-05|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211205010817/https://www.eurogamer.net/articles/2011-07-25-ganon-not-in-zelda-skyward-sword|url-status=live}} Despite his absence, the game suggests that Ganon is a [[reincarnation]] of Demise when Link's companion [[Fi (The Legend of Zelda)|Fi]] says that Demise is "the source of all monsters". Demise's curse also establishes that Ganon, Link and Zelda are placed in an eternal cycle of conflict. Ganon appears in the final boss battle of ''[[A Link Between Worlds]]''. The antagonist Yuga summons him from his seal with the power of the Seven Sages and fuses with Ganon to become a massive creature called Yuga Ganon. In ''[[Breath of the Wild]]'', Ganon gives into malice and hatred to become the malevolent force called Calamity Ganon.{{Cite web |date=2017-08-14 |title=Translation of Zelda: Breath of the Wild's Japanese Ending Prompts Interesting Debate |url=https://www.nintendolife.com/news/2017/08/translation_of_zelda_breath_of_the_wilds_japanese_ending_prompts_interesting_debate |access-date=2023-03-19 |website=Nintendo Life |language=en-GB |archive-date=2023-03-19 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230319182254/https://www.nintendolife.com/news/2017/08/translation_of_zelda_breath_of_the_wilds_japanese_ending_prompts_interesting_debate |url-status=live}} In the backstory, he returns from an earlier defeat to take control of an army of Guardian robots, which he uses against the Hyruleans with the aim of destroying Hyrule. Using his Blight Ganon [[doppelgänger]]s he murders the four Champions who pilot an ancient technology known as the Divine Beasts. He is confined in Hyrule Castle by Zelda's powers until a hundred years later, when Link awakens to prevent his complete destruction of Hyrule.{{Cite web |last=Norman |first=Jim |date=2023-05-16 |title=Zelda: Tears Of The Kingdom: Breath Of The Wild Story Recap |url=https://www.nintendolife.com/guides/zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom-breath-of-the-wild-story-recap |access-date=2023-08-01 |website=Nintendo Life |language=en-GB |archive-date=2023-06-12 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230612163004/https://www.nintendolife.com/guides/zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom-breath-of-the-wild-story-recap |url-status=live}} Ganondorf returns in his humanoid form for the first time since ''Twilight Princess'' in ''[[Tears of the Kingdom]]''.{{Cite web |last=Zollner |first=Amelia |date=2023-04-14 |title=Matt Mercer Confirms He's Voicing Ganon in Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom |url=https://www.ign.com/articles/matt-mercer-confirms-hes-voicing-ganon-in-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom |access-date=2023-04-16 |website=IGN |language=en |archive-date=2023-04-15 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230415203035/https://www.ign.com/articles/matt-mercer-confirms-hes-voicing-ganon-in-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom |url-status=live}} The game's cutscenes reveal that he is present thousands of years in the past when the first king Rauru founded Hyrule. Rauru sacrifices himself to seal Ganondorf beneath Hyrule Castle, where his corpse rots for thousands of years.{{Cite web |last=Greenbaum |first=Aaron |date=2023-05-20 |title=How Tears of the Kingdom Fits Into the Zelda Timeline |url=https://www.denofgeek.com/games/how-tears-of-the-kingdom-fits-into-the-zelda-timeline/ |access-date=2023-05-29 |website=Den of Geek |language=en-US |archive-date=2023-05-29 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230529071918/https://www.denofgeek.com/games/how-tears-of-the-kingdom-fits-into-the-zelda-timeline/ |url-status=live}} He is reawakened in the present when Link and Zelda investigate the depths of Hyrule Castle and, in the confrontation, his power breaks the Master Sword.{{Cite web |last=Watts |first=Steve |date=25 May 2023 |title=Zelda: Tears Of The Kingdom Inverts One Of The Oldest Story Tropes |url=https://www.gamespot.com/articles/zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom-inverts-one-of-the-oldest-story-tropes/1100-6514567/ |access-date=2023-05-29 |website=GameSpot |language=en-US |archive-date=2023-05-28 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230528232022/https://www.gamespot.com/articles/zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom-inverts-one-of-the-oldest-story-tropes/1100-6514567/ |url-status=live}} In the final boss fight, which takes place deep in the chasm beneath Hyrule Castle, he regenerates into his Demon King form. ''Tears of the Kingdom'', a compatible Ganondorf amiibo was released in November 2023.{{Cite web |last=Doolan |first=Liam |date=2023-11-03 |title=Reminder: The New Zelda: Tears Of The Kingdom amiibo based on the final battle from ''Ocarina of Time,'' features a [[Lego minifigure]] of Ganondorf and a brick-built large figure of Ganon in his monstrous boar form.{{Cite news |date=2026-01-16 |title=Zelda: Ocarina of Time Lego set revealed, with a mighty Ganon and hidden hearts |url=https://www.eurogamer.net/zelda-ocarina-of-time-lego-set-leaks-and-ganon-looks-fierce |access-date=2026-03-01 |work=Eurogamer.net |language=en}} ==Reception and legacy== Ganon was one of the first villains in video game history and has been described by critics, including ''[[Guinness World Records Gamer's Edition|Guinness World Records 2013 Gamer's Edition]]''{{Cite web|date=2013-01-23|title=Bowser crowned 'greatest videogame villain of all time' in poll for Guinness World Records 2013 Gamer's Edition|url=https://www.guinnessworldrecords.com/news/2013/1/bowser-crowned-greatest-videogame-villain-of-all-time-in-poll-for-guinness-world-records-2013-gamer%E2%80%99s-edition-46745/?fb_comment_id=493539644020551_5406633|access-date=2021-12-02|website=Guinness World Records|language=en-gb|archive-date=2021-12-02|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211202220559/https://www.guinnessworldrecords.com/news/2013/1/bowser-crowned-greatest-videogame-villain-of-all-time-in-poll-for-guinness-world-records-2013-gamer%E2%80%99s-edition-46745/?fb_comment_id=493539644020551_5406633|url-status=live}} as one of the greatest video game villains.{{Cite web |last=Greenbaum |first=Aaron |date=2022-09-07 |title=The Legend of Zelda: What's the Difference Between Ganon and Ganondorf? |url=https://www.denofgeek.com/games/the-legend-of-zelda-difference-between-ganon-ganondorf/ |access-date=2023-07-24 |website=Den of Geek |language=en-US |archive-date=2023-05-10 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230510173035/https://www.denofgeek.com/games/the-legend-of-zelda-difference-between-ganon-ganondorf/ |url-status=live}}{{Cite web |date=2017-07-27 |title=Our Top 10 Favorite Video Game Villains |url=https://me.ign.com/en/pc/135775/gallery/our-top-10-favorite-video-game-villains |access-date=2023-07-24 |website=IGN |language=en-ae |archive-date=2023-08-30 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230830165949/https://me.ign.com/en/pc/135775/gallery/our-top-10-favorite-video-game-villains |url-status=live}}{{Cite web|last=Staff|first=GamesRadar|date=2018-02-10|title=The best villains in video games|url=https://www.gamesradar.com/villains-in-video-games/|access-date=2021-12-03|website=GamesRadar+|language=en|archive-date=2018-11-26|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181126045653/https://www.gamesradar.com/villains-in-video-games/|url-status=live}}{{cite book|url=http://www.nintendopower.com/images/NP250_250Feature.pdf|title=250 Reasons To Love Nintendo|date=January 2010|publisher=[[Future US]]|volume=250|location=[[South San Francisco, California]]|pages=42, 47|format=Magazine|access-date=2010-07-17|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091229051334/http://nintendopower.com/images/NP250_250Feature.pdf|archive-date=2009-12-29}} Aaron Greenbaum, writing for ''[[Den of Geek]]'', remarked that throughout the series there have been confusing shifts between the characterisation of Ganon and his humanoid counterpart. He noted that in the original game and again in ''Ocarina of Time'', Ganon appears as a mute monster with no dialogue or personality and only exists for the purposes of the gameplay, while in other games his portrayal shifts around. This contrasts with Ganondorf's intelligence and egomaniacal nature, which is emphasised each time the player interacts with him. Jay Castello, writing for ''[[Polygon (website)|Polygon]]'', considered Ganondorf's depiction as an evil character who originates from the desert to have racist undertones that have underpinned his backstory throughout the series.{{Cite web |last=Castello |first=Jay |date=2023-07-22 |title=Tears of the Kingdom's ending is its own kind of tragedy |url=https://www.polygon.com/legend-zelda-tears-kingdom/23802993/loz-totk-ending-zelda-dragon-master-sword-ganondorf |access-date=2023-08-31 |website=Polygon |language=en-US |archive-date=2023-07-23 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230723015844/https://www.polygon.com/legend-zelda-tears-kingdom/23802993/loz-totk-ending-zelda-dragon-master-sword-ganondorf |url-status=live}} Ollie Reynolds of ''[[Nintendo Life]]'' considered Ganondorf's introduction in ''Ocarina of Time'' to be one of the best in gaming and said that, despite being on screen for just a few seconds, his entrance is so well crafted it immediately creates trepidation.{{Cite web |last=Reynolds |first=Ollie |date=2023-11-25 |title=Soapbox: Ganondorf's Villainous Intro In Ocarina Of Time Is One Of Gaming's Best |url=https://www.nintendolife.com/features/soapbox-ganondorfs-villainous-intro-in-ocarina-of-time-is-one-of-gamings-best |access-date=2023-11-26 |website=Nintendo Life |language=en-GB |archive-date=2023-11-26 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231126084530/https://www.nintendolife.com/features/soapbox-ganondorfs-villainous-intro-in-ocarina-of-time-is-one-of-gamings-best |url-status=live}} Following a demo at Space World 2000, ''[[IGN]]'' responded to Ganondorf's character model, highlighting his battle-worn sword and noting that his face was an improvement on the N64 model and represented "the pure evil within". The demo was cancelled by Nintendo and replaced by ''The Wind Waker'' demo at Space World 2001.{{Cite web |last= |first= |last2= |first2= |last3= |first3= |date=2001-01-27 |title=Legend of Zelda (Space World 2000) |url=https://www.ign.com/articles/2001/01/27/legend-of-zelda-space-world-2000 |access-date=2023-07-30 |website=IGN |language=en |archive-date=2023-08-30 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230830165328/https://www.ign.com/articles/2001/01/27/legend-of-zelda-space-world-2000 |url-status=live}} Jose Oteru of ''IGN'' praised Ganondorf's ''Wind Waker'' design, noting its samurai-esque and Eastern influences and describing it as a "visual foil to all of the pirates and sea-driven art direction". He opined that these small design details help to give the character personality.{{Cite web |last=Otero |first=Jose |date=2013-09-17 |title=The Legend of Zelda: The Wind Waker HD Review |url=https://www.ign.com/articles/2013/09/17/the-legend-of-zelda-the-wind-waker-hd-review |access-date=2023-07-24 |website=IGN |language=en |archive-date=2023-08-30 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230830165924/https://www.ign.com/articles/2013/09/17/the-legend-of-zelda-the-wind-waker-hd-review |url-status=live}} Oli Welsh, writing for ''[[Eurogamer]]'', said that the dialogue in the final scenes of ''The Wind Waker'' expresses Ganondorf's motivations and results in a more human villain to which players can more easily relate.{{Cite news |last=Welsh |first=Oli |date=2013-09-17 |title=The Legend of Zelda: The Wind Waker HD review |language=en |work=Eurogamer.net |url=https://www.eurogamer.net/the-legend-of-zelda-the-wind-waker-hd-review |access-date=2023-07-24 |archive-date=2023-07-24 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230724115231/https://www.eurogamer.net/the-legend-of-zelda-the-wind-waker-hd-review |url-status=live}} ''[[GameSpot]]'''s Rob Crossley appreciated the imaginative characterisation of Ganondorf's sidekick Zant in ''Twilight Princess''. While he thought that Nintendo was engaging in "fan service" when they had Ganondorf replace Zant, the final battle between Link and Ganondorf was "symbolic and epic".{{Cite web |last=Crossley |first=Rob |title=The Legend of Zelda: Twilight Princess HD Review |url=https://www.gamespot.com/reviews/the-legend-of-zelda-twilight-princess-hd-review/1900-6416369/ |access-date=2023-07-24 |website=GameSpot |language=en-US |archive-date=2023-06-16 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230616231007/https://www.gamespot.com/reviews/the-legend-of-zelda-twilight-princess-hd-review/1900-6416369/ |url-status=live}} In a review of ''Breath of the Wild'', Kyle Hilliard, writing for ''[[Game Informer]]'', considered that Calamity Ganon's threatening presence, seen from any vantage point in the game's world, creates a tangible goal that makes the final effort to defeat him seem like "the culmination of a lifetime of preparation" and makes the finale more rewarding.{{Cite magazine |last=Hilliard |first=Kyle |date=1 March 2017 |title=The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild Review - A New Era Dawns On Zelda |url=https://www.gameinformer.com/games/the_legend_of_zelda_breath_of_the_wild/b/switch/archive/2017/03/02/game-informer-the-legend-of-zelda-breath-of-the-wild-switch-review.aspx |access-date=2023-07-23 |magazine=Game Informer |language=en |archive-date=2023-07-23 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230723224744/https://www.gameinformer.com/games/the_legend_of_zelda_breath_of_the_wild/b/switch/archive/2017/03/02/game-informer-the-legend-of-zelda-breath-of-the-wild-switch-review.aspx |url-status=live}} [[File:Ganondorf artwork for Tears of the Kingdom.png|thumb|right|upright=1|alt=Artwork of Ganondorf in ''Tears of the Kingdom'' depicting his Gerudo form and his Demon King form |Ganondorf's design in ''[[The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom]]'' received widespread praise from critics and gamers.]] Anticipation grew for the return of Ganondorf with the release of the third trailer for ''Tears of the Kingdom'' in April 2023, due to him being absent for almost 17 years since ''Twilight Princess''.{{Cite web |last=Cryer |first=Hirun |date=2023-04-13 |title=The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom fans are already worshipping Ganondorf |url=https://www.gamesradar.com/the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom-fans-are-already-worshipping-ganondorf/ |access-date=2023-07-26 |website=GamesRadar+ |language=en |archive-date=2023-07-26 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230726202737/https://www.gamesradar.com/the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom-fans-are-already-worshipping-ganondorf/ |url-status=live}} This incarnation of Ganondorf received widespread praise for his sex appeal,{{Cite web |last=Hague |first=Alana |date=2023-04-13 |title=Random: Of Course People Are Thirsty For Ganondorf In Zelda: Tears Of The Kingdom |url=https://www.nintendolife.com/news/2023/04/random-of-course-people-are-thirsty-for-ganondorf-in-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom |access-date=2023-04-20 |website=Nintendo Life |language=en-GB |archive-date=2023-04-20 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230420012459/https://www.nintendolife.com/news/2023/04/random-of-course-people-are-thirsty-for-ganondorf-in-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom |url-status=live}}{{Cite web |last=McWhertor |first=Michael |date=2023-04-13 |title=Ganondorf is back in Tears of the Kingdom, and he's hotter than ever |url=https://www.polygon.com/23681806/zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom-ganondorf-artwork-hot |access-date=2023-04-20 |website=Polygon |language=en-US |archive-date=2023-04-20 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230420122734/https://www.polygon.com/23681806/zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom-ganondorf-artwork-hot |url-status=live}} with Jenni Lada of ''[[Siliconera]]'' commenting that this added more mystery to the character by making him appear "charismatic and charming" rather than just an evil villain.{{Cite web |last=Lada |first=Jenni |date=2023-04-19 |title=It's Easy to See the Appeal of Tears of the Kingdom Ganondorf |url=https://www.siliconera.com/easy-to-see-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom-rehydrated-ganondorf-appeal/ |access-date=2023-07-22 |website=Siliconera |language=en-US |archive-date=2023-07-22 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230722131546/https://www.siliconera.com/easy-to-see-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom-rehydrated-ganondorf-appeal/ |url-status=live}} Carolyn Petit of ''[[Kotaku]]'' considered Ganondorf's characterisation in ''Tears of the Kingdom'' to be disappointing, describing him as a "one-note character...without any real character or moral texture". She opined that this results in the game squandering the sense of loss that resonates at its beginning and is in contrast to his more compelling appearance in ''The Wind Waker''.{{Cite web |last=Petit |first=Carolyn |date=2023-06-23 |title=The Legend Of Zelda: Tears Of The Kingdom: The Kotaku Review |url=https://kotaku.com/the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom-the-kotaku-r-1850570840 |access-date=2023-07-24 |website=Kotaku |language=en |archive-date=2023-07-24 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230724110258/https://kotaku.com/the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom-the-kotaku-r-1850570840 |url-status=live}} Jim Norman of ''[[Nintendo Life]]'' thought that Nintendo needs to do more with Ganondorf's character depth, as his appearances throughout the series follow a common narrative structure where he is largely absent until the final battle.{{Cite web |last=Norman |first=Jim |date=2023-10-05 |title=Soapbox: TOTK's Ganondorf Is Great, But Zelda Needs To Do More With Its Villain |url=https://www.nintendolife.com/features/soapbox-totks-ganondorf-is-great-but-zelda-needs-to-do-more-with-its-villain |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231006075139/https://www.nintendolife.com/features/soapbox-totks-ganondorf-is-great-but-zelda-needs-to-do-more-with-its-villain |archive-date=6 October 2023 |access-date=2023-10-30 |website=Nintendo Life |language=en-GB}} The boss fights between Link and Ganon have received a mixed reception. Mark Langshaw of ''[[Digital Spy]]'' considered ''Ocarina of Time'' to be one of the most memorable boss battles in gaming, commenting that the dual contest against Ganondorf and Ganon offers "two epic boss battles for the price of one".{{Cite web|last=Langshaw|first=Mark|date=2012-01-29|title=Feature: Most Memorable Boss Battles|url=http://www.digitalspy.com/videogames/a362471/feature-most-memorable-boss-battles/|access-date=2021-12-03|website=Digital Spy|language=en-GB|archive-date=2021-12-03|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211203152303/https://www.digitalspy.com/videogames/a362471/feature-most-memorable-boss-battles/|url-status=live}} Chris Freiburg for ''Den of Geek'' also chose it as the best boss fight, describing Ganon as "a towering pig beast wielding two massive swords in an arena surrounded by a ring of fire" and opined, "it's hard not to consider it the best boss fight in franchise history".{{Cite web|last=Freiburg|first=Chris|date=2021-07-17|title=15 Best Legend of Zelda Boss Fights Ever|url=https://www.denofgeek.com/games/best-legend-of-zelda-boss-fights-ever/|url-status=live|access-date=2021-12-27|website=Den of Geek|language=en-US|archive-date=2021-12-27|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211227184557/https://www.denofgeek.com/games/best-legend-of-zelda-boss-fights-ever/}} Brian Shea, writing for ''Game Informer'', chose the boss battle in ''The Wind Waker'' as the greatest moment, stating the final blow "is in stark contrast to the cute cel-shaded visual style in the best way possible", which "delivers players one of the most memorable final sequences in gaming".{{Cite magazine|last=Shea|first=Brian|title=The Best Ganons Ranked|url=https://www.gameinformer.com/2023/05/19/ranking-every-ganon-in-the-legend-of-zelda-series|access-date=2021-12-02|magazine=Game Informer|language=en|archive-date=2021-12-02|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211202211519/https://www.gameinformer.com/b/features/archive/2017/04/06/the-best-ganons-ranked-legend-of-zelda.aspx|url-status=live}} Marco Vito Oddo of ''[[Collider (website)|Collider]]'' also considered this as the best Ganondorf duel and compared it to the final boss battle in ''Breath of the Wild'', which he described as "another giant blob of dark energy that fights just like every other Ganon Blight the player already fought and defeated" and "an unsatisfactory ending to a fantastic game".{{Cite web|last=Vito Oddo|first=Marco|date=2021-08-17|title=All 'The Legend of Zelda' Ganondorf / Ganon Battles, Ranked|url=https://collider.com/zelda-ganon-fights-ranked/|url-status=live|access-date=2021-12-03|website=Collider|language=en-US|archive-date=2021-12-03|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211203110223/https://collider.com/zelda-ganon-fights-ranked/}} Julian Benson of ''[[TechRadar]]'' noted the extreme difficulty of the final boss fight against Demon King Ganondorf in ''Tears of the Kingdom'', but felt that the game does not prepare the player with the right skillset to successfully defeat him, resulting in him being "the wrong final boss" for the finale.{{Cite web |last=Benson |first=Julian |date=2023-05-15 |title=The Legend of Zelda:
